stories.title: Kon Knueppel, Coby White out for Hornets' season opener
stories.summary: The Hornets will be without guards Kon Knueppel and Coby White as well as veteran forward Grant Williams as they open their season Wednesday at Brooklyn.
stories.detailText: The Charlotte Hornets will be without guards Kon Knueppel and Coby White as well as veteran forward Grant Williams as they open their season Wednesday at the Brooklyn Nets . Knueppel, who was the first rookie to lead the league with 273 made 3-pointers last season, injured his left hamstring during offseason on-court activity and missed the entire preseason. White suffered a left calf strain Oct. 5 during training camp and missed the remainder of preseason. Williams was ruled out for all four of Charlotte's preseason games because of a right hamstring injury. The team said Tuesday that all three players have resumed individual on-court activity. The Hornets are hoping to rely on Knueppel and White this season after trading LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves over the summer. Knueppel averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 42.5% 3-point shooting as a rookie. The Hornets acquired White from the Chicago Bulls in February, and he went on to have a strong finish to the season with his new team. He was the hero in the team's play-in victory over the Miami Heat , scoring 19 points and hitting the turnaround 3 late in regulation to force overtime. He signed a three-year, $74 million contract with Charlotte over the summer. Williams has averaged 7.2 points and 3.7 rebounds per game during his seven seasons.

stories.title: Five St. John’s men’s basketball alumni make NBA opening day rosters
stories.summary: Zuby Ejiofor, Dillon Mitchell, and Bryce Hopkins become the latest ex-Johnnies to join The Association.

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Babineau/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images As the NBA regular season officially tips off on Tuesday, the Red Storm will have their most representation in the Association in decades. Five former St. John’s men’s basketball players made opening day rosters this year, including the Red Storm’s three-man rookie class of Zuby Ejiofor, Dillon Mitchell, and Bryce Hopkins. The Red Storm’s All-Big East frontcourt trio were all selected in the 2026 NBA draft, marking the first time in the two-round era that three St. John’s players were selected in the same NBA draft. Zuby Ejiofor ended the program’s 11-year draftless drought when the Atlanta Hawks selected him with the 23rd overall pick in the first round. Dillon Mitchell and Bryce Hopkins went off the board in the second round with the 40th overall selection by the Boston Celtics and the 49th overall selection by the Denver Nuggets, respectively. As a first-round pick, Ejiofor is on a guaranteed contract and is expected to battle for frontcourt minutes off the bench with fellow rookie Henri Veesaar, Jock Landale, Asa Newell, and Mouhamed Gueye, while Mitchell and Hopkins are on two-way deals and will likely split time between the NBA and the G-League. Zuby LOB ✈️ pic.twitter.com/LKtZvdx9EO — Atlanta Hawks (@ATLHawks) October 12, 2026 Julian Champagnie, the most experienced Red Storm alum in the league, is set to begin his fifth professional season with the reigning Western Conference champion San Antonio Spurs. After the Philadelphia 76ers waived him midway through his rookie year, the undrafted Brooklyn native quickly found a home deep in Texas and has served as the Spurs’ 3-and-D weapon ever since. Last season with the Spurs, Champagnie was one of 18 NBA players to play all 82 of their regular-season games. He averaged a career-best 11.1 points and 5.8 rebounds on 43.7% shooting from the field and 38.1% from deep. On New Year’s Eve, he set the Spurs franchise record for most threes made in a game with eleven treys in a 134-132 win over the Knicks. The former All-Big East Most Improved Player award winner started all 23 playoff games for the Spurs in his postseason debut last season, including all five NBA Finals games, becoming the first St. John’s alum to play on the sport’s biggest stage since Ron Artest (a.k.a. Metta World Peace) won the championship with the Lakers in 2010. 5 TRIPLES IN THE FIRST HALF FOR JULIAN CHAMPAGNIE 👌 HE'S GOT 15. SPURS LEAD BY 7 AT THE BREAK OF GAME 1. pic.twitter.com/gPn0bhFTsM — NBA (@NBA) June 4, 2026 Unfortunately for Champagnie (and luckily for many Johnnies fans around New York), the Spurs blew double-digit leads in all four losses to the eventual champion Knicks, including a 29-point advantage in Game 4— the largest comeback in NBA Finals history . During the offseason, Champagnie inked a new three-year, $45 million contract that will keep him with the San Antonio Spurs through the 2028-29 season. He might lose his starting power forward spot to new addition Tobias Harris once the 34-year-old veteran returns from injury, but Champagnie will still be a key contributor for a serious title contender. Like Champagnie, Daniss Jenkins entered the league as an undrafted rookie and cut his teeth in the G-League before he could solidify a role with a playoff contender. Jenkins is entering his third season in the NBA and his second with a full-time role with the Detroit Pistons. After making only seven appearances as a rookie, the Texas native became Cade Cunningham’s backup at point guard, logging 9.3 points and 3.9 assists per game across 72 contests and 19 starts for the Pistons, who finished as the No. 1 seed in the East. Back in February, the Pistons upgraded Jenkins’s two-way contract to a two-year, $8 million standard NBA deal. Jenkins had some clutch moments in his first taste of playoff basketball. He sank a buzzer-beating triple to end the third quarter as part of a 16-point, 5-assist performance in Game 7 of their first-round series to help the Pistons complete a 3-1 series comeback. He then averaged double figures and started his first-ever playoff Game 7 against the Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Semifinals, though the Pistons were knocked out in an inauspicious 31-point loss in that game. DANISS JENKINS AT THE 3Q BUZZER 🚨 DETROIT IS LOVING IT 🔥 pic.twitter.com/IC0DCKpEXW — ESPN (@espn) May 3, 2026 The Pistons exercised Jenkins’s $4 million team option to keep him for the 2026-27 season. He’ll continue to play as the first point guard off the bench and could earn more starting opportunities at two-guard this season. Other Red Storm alumni who could spend time in the league include Kadary Richmond, Aaron Scott, and Deivon Smith, who were teammates on the 2025 Big East champion squad and played in this July’s NBA Summer League. Richmond made his NBA debut last season with the Washington Wizards, but spent most of his time with the G-League’s Capital City Go-Go before the Cavaliers traded him to their G-League affiliate, the Canton Charge; the Cavaliers then waived him in the preseason. Scott most recently earned a training camp deal with the Brooklyn Nets, then was waived and will likely play for their G-League Team, the Long Island Nets. The same has been done for Smith, who was signed and then waived by the Golden State Warriors in hopes of keeping him on their G-League team.

stories.title: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa to miss Wizards season opener with ankle injury
stories.summary: He is day-to-day according to coach Brian Keefe, meaning he could make his debut this weekend.
stories.detailText: The AJ Dybantsa Rookie of the Year train will not leave the station on time Wednesday. Dybantsa will miss the Wizards' opener against the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday with a tweaked ankle, coach Brian Keefe told reporters . He added that Dybantsa is day-to-day going forward. The Wizards have a back-to-back over the weekend, hosting Toronto on Friday then traveling to Chicago on Saturday. The Wizards selected Dybantsa with the No. 1 overall pick, and hopes are high that he can be a catalyst to help turn a long-struggling franchise around. After an impressive Summer League, Dybantsa was still finding his footing in the preseason, averaging 12.8 points per game on 43.9% shooting, and just 18.2% from 3-point range. Dybantsa is paired with All-Stars Trae Young and Anthony Davis to start his rookie season, and there is debate around the league about whether or not this is good for his development. Scouts were divided about the idea, as they detailed to Josh Robbins in a fantastic story at The Athletic . Some scouts said it would be a "massive positive" not to have Dybantsa carry so much of the load and that he can figure out the game without having to create a ton of offense. Another scout felt this way: "Ideally, you put the ball in his hands, and you let him figure it out," one scout said. "He's talented enough that, as you grow your team, he'll get better... It can certainly kind of hinder some aspects of his development, him being better as a creator. If he doesn't have those opportunities, if he's kind of boxed into spacing the floor and not being like a knockdown shooter, he would benefit from having the ball, posting up smaller guys, driving, getting into the teeth of the defense." For the Wizards, it's about starting to win more now, not waiting for Dybantsa and the Wizards' other key young players — Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson — to figure it out. Young and Davis help this team win games now. Dybantsa won't be figuring anything out on opening night, he'll be in street clothes.

stories.title: Saliou Niang, former NBA Draft pick, cleared to compete for LSU, which has given up RJ Luis Jr. eligibility fight: Reports
stories.summary: Last year, Niang was picked in the second round, whereas Luis went undrafted.
stories.detailText: LSU men's basketball is once again led by head coach Will Wade, who is in his second stint at the helm of the program after stays at McNeese and NC State. Tyler Kaufman via Getty Images Reports on Tuesday provided a bit more clarity about what the first iteration of Will Wade's Tigers will look like during his second stint as LSU head coach. On one hand, LSU will have the services of former NBA Draft pick Saliou Niang, who, according to multiple reports , has been cleared to compete for the Tigers this season. On the other hand, per CBS Sports' Matt Norlander , LSU has given up its fight for former St. John's star RJ Luis Jr. to be eligible. BREAKING: Saliou Niang has been cleared to compete for the LSU Tigers, his representatives, Sead Galijasevic and Andrea Grossi, told DraftExpress. Niang was cleared by the NCAA eligibility process and is now officially eligible to suit up for LSU under head coach Will Wade. pic.twitter.com/6hpRJNTkIF — Jonathan Givony (@DraftExpress) October 20, 2026 Whereas Niang was picked in the second round of the 2025 draft, Luis went undrafted last year. That said, Luis signed contracts with the Utah Jazz and the Boston Celtics. As a result, he's now prohibited from joining an SEC member institution, according to the conference's recently adopted policy , which notably bans basketball players, among others, who previously signed with an NBA or G League team . So, even though a preliminary injunction in a Louisiana court reportedly paved the way for Luis to play , the SEC's rules stood between him and the LSU roster. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Norlander reported Tuesday that, privately, Wade had been confident that Luis, 23, would eventually be permitted to take the court for LSU, "but the SEC would not budge." Will Wade had been privately confident for months that Luis would eventually find his way to play, but the SEC would not budge. Sources tell CBS Sports that, in recent days, Wade has come to accept the reality that Luis would not be allowed to compete for LSU this season. — Matt Norlander (@MattNorlander) October 20, 2026 Luis, a 6-foot-7 wing who averaged 18.2 points for St. John's en route to earning Big East Player of the Year honors during the 2024-25 campaign, hasn't played in an NBA regular-season game. Neither has the 22-year-old Niang. The Cleveland Cavaliers selected him in the second round of last year's draft with the No. 58 overall pick. Although Cleveland kept his NBA rights, Niang returned to Europe, this time to play for Italian club Virtus Bologna. The Senegalese-Italian forward, per Norlander , got the green light to suit up for LSU because Niang's decision to attend LSU was made before NCAA policy was enacted that would make him ineligible. Furthermore, as reported by Norlander, Niang's decision was pre-enrollment, unlike Luis'. The NCAA reportedly decided it wasn't fair to apply its new rule retroactively, and the SEC is abiding by that NCAA ruling. Niang posted 7.1 points per contest in 38 EuroLeague games last season. He's the latest piece to a head-scratching puzzle that Wade is attempting to put together before his first season back at the helm of an LSU program he first spearheaded from 2017-22. After stays at McNeese and NC State, Wade is trying to pull off an unorthodox roster construction at LSU, testing the limits during the NCAA's eligibility crisis . Niang is one of a handful of international players the Tigers have eyed for their 2026-27 roster. Croatian center Michael Ruzic, 20, has also been cleared to play for them. Another big man, 23-year-old Brice Dessert from France, will soon be good to go as well, according to Norlander.

stories.title: 26 former Kentucky Wildcats are on NBA rosters for the 2026-27 season
stories.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns and the defending NBA champion New York Knicks lead the way for former Cats in the association.
stories.detailText: The 2026-27 NBA season is here, and 26 former Kentucky Basketball players are on opening day rosters. That’s the most of any college program and is the 15th straight season in which the Wildcats led the way. Kentucky has at least one player on 19 of 30 NBA teams. The Oklahoma City Thunder and the San Antonio Spurs lead the way with three Wildcats on their rosters, while the Philadelphia 76ers, Miami Heat and Houston Rockets each have two. This past season, Karl-Anthony Towns won an NBA championship with the New York Knicks, while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander won his second consecutive NBA MVP award, which came a year after he won a title with the Thunder. Here’s to hoping for another banner year for former Wildcats in the NBA! stories.title: Silver: LeBron's helicopter travel 'perfectly appropriate'
stories.summary: The helicopter used by Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James to commute from New York is "perfectly appropriate," NBA commissioner Adam Silver said on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Tuesday.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK -- The helicopter used by 76ers forward LeBron James to commute to Philadelphia from New York is "perfectly appropriate," NBA commissioner Adam Silver said on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Tuesday. "He has a deal with Fanatics," Silver said. "It's perfectly appropriate if part of his deal is they're going to supply a helicopter to him as long as it's just a deal between the Fanatics and LeBron and no team is involved; there's no rules issue there whatsoever." After signing with the Sixers in free agency, James decided to live in New York -- a decision Sixers players have made before him, including his former coach, JJ Redick -- but James' choice to travel by helicopter has made headlines. During news conferences after practice, players often pause and laugh as James' helicopter is heard exiting from the roof of the team's business center, drowning out the sound in the facility. James recently brushed off the added attention to his travel method. "I've done it before; just another way of transportation," he said.

stories.title: Windhorst: What playing at Madison Square Garden means to LeBron James
stories.summary: It's only fitting that LeBron opens his final chapter inside "The World's Most Famous Arena."
stories.detailText: Mike Brown peered up at the Madison Square Garden crowd, sensing exactly what it wanted. So, with 10 seconds remaining in a 14-point game, the head coach rushed in a substitution so his starter could receive a well-earned standing ovation from New York Knicks fans. It was a 50-point, 10-rebound, eight-assist performance that finished with a killer fourth quarter to ensure the victory in a moment the player seemed born to embrace. That game was played March 5, 2008, in Brown's third season at the helm of the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers -- and 18 years before he would guide the Knicks to the NBA title in June. That player was a 23-year-old LeBron James . "I've dreamed about playing well in this building," James said, with a glint in his eye, after the 2008 tilt. "To get a standing ovation at the best basketball arena in the world, it's one of the best things that's ever happened to me." You can understand why, after witnessing all this, the Knicks' front office personnel had stars in their eyes and No. 23 on their minds. (The Cavs had even obtained permission, at James' request, to wear their alternate navy blue jerseys to match the debut of his Nike LeBron V "Yankees" colorway .) Less than a week following James' performance, Knicks team president Donnie Walsh hired Mike D'Antoni as New York's newest coach with the explicit purpose to draw James in. On James' next visit to New York, in November 2008, he called D'Antoni "an offensive mastermind," and Knicks front office staffers might've passed out for a few moments. Cleveland's front office crew, meanwhile, swallowed rather hard. That praise aside, the Knicks were already convinced James wanted to make Madison Square Garden his next home, so much so that they threw caution to the wind. Just days prior, Walsh traded key players Jamal Crawford and Zach Randolph to clear the necessary cap room to sign James -- a full 19 months before he was set to hit free agency. That, of course, didn't happen. James, as you might recall, took his talents south. On Tuesday night , Brown, Jalen Brunson and the rest of the Knicks will receive their championship rings and a banner will be unveiled in a moment that will add to the lore of "The World's Most Famous Arena." It's fitting that James -- now with Tuesday's opponents, the Philadelphia 76ers -- will be on hand for the festivities. Including the playoffs, James is 28-11 at MSG in his career and has averaged 28 points, seven rebounds and seven assists per game. Those are close to his career averages, but behind them sits a giant file of moments on the Garden floor. In addition to two 50-point games, James has 12 30-plus-point games at MSG. Which is why over the years James has repeatedly said things like this, from 2015: "I wish I could play 82 games a year here. Because it's the mecca of basketball. You get a great feeling when you walk in there because there is so much history." By then, Knicks fans might have thought he was being a little patronizing. Since draft lottery night in 2003, when New York had the ninth-best odds but huge dreams, the Knicks and their fans coveted James. An argument could be made that the Knicks would've moved mountains to get to James virtually every year from 2003 to 2025. Which makes it ironic that James told ESPN last month that he, perhaps for the first time, actually wanted to be a Knick this year. It was driven, at least in part, by the concept of playing his home games at MSG. "I had visions of playing in the Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN's Dave McMenamin at 76ers media day. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio , I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." For the first time in 25 years, the Knicks and their returning championship core could honestly say they didn't need him. He will have to settle for another Garden memory. This will be the fifth time James has had to endure another team's banner night, but this one might feel a bit different. James already has graduated to the point where he looks at every trip to MSG as perhaps his last. "No matter [when] it is, it's going to be like, 'S---, I'll never play again in Madison Square Garden,'" James said when he visited with the Los Angeles Lakers in February. "It's been a wide range of an importance of people to grace this floor, and I hope I have a little, small snippet of somebody that came through here." James has been contemplating the possibility of playing his final game at MSG for several years now, making each visit a potential seminal moment. But that's one of the features of his career: It keeps going. While Tuesday's matchup at the Garden is one of the biggest early games on the calendar , there's always the possibility of an additional meeting between the Knicks and the Sixers at MSG in the NBA Cup before another high-profile game there in February . And it should be pointed out that New York and Philadelphia have met in two of the past three postseasons; a few more springtime showdowns in the Garden would shock no one. So, if opening night is the beginning of James' goodbye to Madison Square Garden, it could be a lengthy embrace.

Steph Curry limps off the court at open practice and he just went back to the locker room @NBCSWarriors Real quiet in here now pic.twitter.com/cLEFcOwTGt — Dalton Johnson (@DaltonJ_Johnson) October 18, 2026 Although the scene itself suggested Curry might’ve injured the same knee that kept him out for roughly a third of the 2025-26 season, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr clarified Curry tweaked his ankle and is “fine.” Steve Kerr said he talked to Steph after practice and said “he’s fine.” Kerr said it was an ankle tweak, not the knee. pic.twitter.com/i0UPFZdYsw — Nick Friedell (@NickFriedell) October 18, 2026 Kerr said Curry practiced Monday morning and is expected to play Wednesday against the Lakers. Last season, he averaged 26.6 points, 4.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.1 steals while shooting 39.3% beyond the arc and 58.4% on 2-pointers, the latter of which was the third-highest mark of his career. He’s still the league’s preeminent shooter whose vast long-range talents, movement, quick decision-making and motor constantly stress defenses like nobody else around the league can. Assuming he plays, his presence will certainly test a revamped Lakers defense, with the likes of Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams all presumably getting chances to try and slow Curry down. It’ll be interesting to see how the Lakers dole out all their defensive assignments Wednesday night. The Warriors are not a big team but the forward tandem of Draymond Green and Yaxel Lendeborg will still be beefier than whoever Los Angeles starts alongside Grimes. I imagine Al Horford starts at center but the Lakers may prefer to keep Walker Kessler inside as much as possible and let him roam off of Green, though that comes with risks, given Curry and Green’s two-man connection. Nonetheless, the Warriors should have their own challenges figuring out how to adequately slow both Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, so the entire chess match between Kerr and JJ Redick could be quite fascinating throughout Wednesday’s matchup. And the NBA is always more fun when Curry is healthy doing his preposterous Curry things, so it’s nice to hear he should be available, even if it makes the Lakers’ lives harder. stories.title: Celtics announce starting lineup before opening game against Pistons
stories.summary: Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Jayson Tatum, Paul George, and Mitchell Robinson will start for the Celtics in their first game of the year.
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MI - JANUARY 19: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons plays defense during the game against Derrick White #9 of the Boston Celtics on January 19, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images DETROIT — The Celtics will start Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Jayson Tatum, Paul George, and Mitchell Robinson in their Opening Day game against the Detroit Pistons. In the Celtics’ two full-strength preseason games, Joe Mazzulla started the same five-person squad. The team went 4-0 in the preseason and finished first in net rating, defensive rating, and rebounding percentage. The Pistons, meanwhile, will start Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins, and Jalen Duren. Joe Mazzulla stressed pregame that he thinks too much stock is put into the starting lineup “In all honesty, I think people care about it too much — it lasts five minutes,” Mazzulla said. “There’s still 43 minutes left in the game. end-of-quarter lineups are important, start-to-quarter lineups are important, end-of-game lineups are important. So I think it just gets overblown.” Mazzulla explained that he gameplans lots of different lineups for different in-game situations, and that all are equally important. “I put in just as much thought as I do as an end-of-line-up as I would a starting lineup, versus an end-to-half lineup, versus a lineup when you’re winning, a lineup when you’re losing, a need-three lineup,” he said. “There’s 10 different lineups, so they all carry the same weight to me.” Mazzulla also noted that the starting lineup on Opening Night rarely holds throughout the entirety of the season. “The year is 82 games,” Mazzulla said. “It’s a long year. I guarantee you tonight’s won’t be the same one for 82 games. But, I put just as much stock in the other 9 lineups that we may or may not need to go to within a particular game.” Payton Pritchard, for one, isn’t worried about coming off the bench At practice on Monday, Payton Pritchard, the 2025 Sixth Man of the Year, made it clear he wasn’t concerned about starting. “To me, a starter is the amount of minutes you play,” he said. “Do you finish games? Are you playing 30-plus minutes? Then you are a starter.” “How you impact the game is what really matters to me. I don’t really care. This might be an ego thing — like I don’t really care to hear my name called at the beginning of the game. The first five minutes of the game really have no effect on the game.” Last year, when at full strength, the team started Derrick White, Sam Hauser, Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum, and Neemias Queta. Hauser started 49 games, but Jordan Walsh (25 games), Baylor Scheierman (20 games), Ron Harper Jr. (3 games), and Hugo Gonzalez (3 games) also got opportunities to start at the wing spot.

stories.title: The King of Cool: P&T’s interview with Walt “Clyde” Frazier
stories.summary: Clyde reads Posting & Toasting!
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JUNE 08: Former New York Knicks player Walt Frazier poses prior to Game Three between the New York Knicks and the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on June 08, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you were to look up the words cool , stylish , flair , and all-time great in the dictionary, you would find four distinct definitions, each describing a quality that few individuals can truly embody. Cool: Very fashionable, impressive, or appealing in a way that is universally admired. Stylish: Possessing a high degree of quality in appearance, design, or behavior. Flair: A natural talent or ability to do things in an original, stylish, and captivating manner. All-Time Great: An individual regarded among the very best to ever perform in a particular field, sport, or profession. What’s missing alongside each of these definitions in the dictionary is a picture of Walt “Clyde” Frazier. Throughout the storied history of the NBA, countless legends have left their mark on the game, but few, if any, have embodied all four qualities quite like Frazier. From his legendary playing days with the New York Knicks in the 1970s to his continued presence as one of the most recognizable personalities in basketball more than five decades later, Frazier remains in a class of his own, both on and off the court. A man whose legendary style extends far beyond his flamboyant wardrobe, Frazier helped define an era of New York basketball, captivating fans with his effortless cool, unparalleled court vision, tenacious defense, and undeniable flair. Widely regarded as one of the greatest players in New York Knicks franchise history, Frazier’s place among basketball royalty is unquestionable. A two-time NBA champion, seven-time NBA All-Star, and member of both the NBA’s 50th and 75th Anniversary Teams, his legacy is as timeless as the city he helped bring to basketball prominence. Simply put, there has never been another Walt “Clyde” Frazier. And chances are, there never will be. Let’s start with his style. Clyde’s style was unlike anybody else’s in the NBA during the ‘70s, and to this day, there still hasn’t been a close second. As a young man in his twenties, Frazier became just as recognizable for driving around New York City in his custom Rolls-Royce while sporting a full-length mink coat and fedora as he was for his play on the court. Today, his fashion sense remains as distinctive as ever. Throughout a broadcasting career spanning nearly 40 years, including almost 30 as a television commentator for MSG and the Knicks, his wardrobe has remained unmistakable, from tiger-print suits to custom blazers reminiscent of Joseph’s Technicolor Dreamcoat. There arguably hasn’t been a more fashionable icon in the NBA’s nearly 80-year history. (Original Caption) NEW YORK: Apparently determined to match his flashy drives on the basketball court with some equally flashy driving, New York Knicks' star guard Walt Frazier gets set for a spin in his sleek Rolls Royce. For the fourth straight year, Frazier was named Jan. 9 as a starter on the East team in the NBA all-star game to be played in Chicago Jan. 23. Frazier was a trendsetter, one of the first NBA players to truly express his personality through his wardrobe, at a time when players were largely known for what they did on the court rather than what they wore off it. His style became a part of his identity, both during his playing days and throughout his broadcasting career, setting him apart from his contemporaries and the generations of NBA stars who followed. So, just how did Walt Frazier become Clyde? “Coming to the Mecca. New York City. Fashion, passion,” Frazier explains. “When we played, we wore suits and ties to the game. We were always trying to outdress each other. Our idols were The Temptations, The Four Tops. So we emulated the way these guys performed.” As Frazier recalls, the influence of Motown played a significant role in shaping his style, much like hip-hop has influenced today’s NBA players. “Today you see the guys dressed like the rappers… our style was created from Motown. And I took it to another level with the Clyde. One day I bought this wide-brimmed hat and I wore it to the game and everybody go, hey, look at Clyde. And I used to steal the ball on the court.” But the nickname would eventually become much more than just a reflection of his wardrobe. “Then I was blessed enough to be the first guy to endorse a sneaker, the Puma Clyde in 1973. So that was the evolution of the mink coat, the Rolls Royce. So it was just my being around New York and observing people watching the Clyde persona personified.” On the court, Clyde helped lead the Knicks to their first two NBA championships in 1970 and 1973, with the greatest performance of his career coming in Game 7 of the 1970 NBA Finals. With the championship on the line, Frazier delivered one of the most memorable performances in NBA Finals history, scoring 36 points, dishing out a Game 7-record 19 assists, grabbing seven rebounds, and sinking all 12 of his free throws to help secure the Knicks’ first NBA title. NEW YORK, NEW YORK – MAY 04, 1970: Walt Frazier #10 of the New York Knicks drives against Jerry West #44 of the Los Angeles Lakers during Game Five of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on May 04, 1970 in New York, New York. (Photo by James Drake/Getty Images) | Getty Images While Clyde’s performance in Game 7 ultimately helped lead the Knicks to their first-ever NBA championship, Clyde and his teammates also received some unexpected motivation from their captain, Willis Reed, who, despite battling a severe leg injury, famously limped onto the court just before tipoff. “People thought it was premeditated, but we did not know he was coming. So when we came on the court, we were just as flabbergasted as everybody else when we saw him.” Frazier recalls how Reed’s unexpected appearance immediately changed the team’s confidence. “By seeing him, it gave us so much confidence. And obviously, he started the game. He made his first two shots. And I thought the Lakers were psyched out from that point, and I would have the game of my life.” With two NBA championships, seven All-Star appearances, four All-NBA First Team selections, and numerous other accolades to his name, Frazier was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1987. His No. 10 jersey also hangs in the rafters of Madison Square Garden, making him one of just eight Knicks players to have their numbers retired by the franchise. But while Frazier’s playing days eventually came to an end, his connection to the Knicks and Madison Square Garden was far from over. In 1987, Clyde began a new chapter with the organization, trading his sneakers for a microphone as he transitioned into broadcasting, where his unmistakable personality and signature style would once again make him a fixture in New York basketball. Clyde became famous for his iconic on-air rhymes, including “razzlin’ and dazzlin’” and “posting and toasting,” the latter of which inspired the name of our very own website. Frazier explained that his signature rhymes developed naturally as he gained experience in broadcasting and began to understand the nuances of being a color commentator. “The play-by-play guy does most of the talking on radio. So in order to get into sometimes what I had to say, I had to use rhymes and, you know, that’s how I started doing it.” With our website’s name paying tribute to one of Clyde’s most recognizable catchphrases, it was only fitting to ask him what he thought about Posting and Toasting. “Yeah, I read you all the time. I enjoy it, man. It’s very good.” With the Knicks winning their first championship since 1973, when Clyde hoisted his second trophy, Frazier reflected on the similarities between his championship teams and the current roster. “It’s an uncanny comparison, man. We personify a team. You can’t mention Frazier without Bradley, without Reed, without Barnett. Same thing with this team. You can’t mention Brunson without Hart, without Bridges, without KAT, without OG. So they personify a team. They’re very unselfish. They like each other. And it’s manifested in the way they play the game.” And when asked which player from the Knicks’ 2026 championship roster would have fit in best alongside his former teammates, Clyde didn’t hesitate to name the Heart of the City, Josh Hart, pointing to his versatility and physical style of play. “(Hart) rebounds, he defends, he scores, he plays with reckless abandon. So he would be that type of guy that would fit in our era, which was more physical. You know, we could hand check, push guys around the court. So I think Hart would be perfect for that era.” NEW YORK, NY – FEBRUARY 6: Josh Hart #3 and Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks congratulate Walt Frazier and Mike Breen on 25 years of broadcasting before the game against the Memphis Grizzlies on February 6, 2024 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2024 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images As the 2026-27 NBA season tips off on Tuesday, October 20, with the players receiving their championship rings and the Knicks raising their third championship banner to the Madison Square Garden rafters, Clyde is teaming up with Spike Lee and AT&T for a special celebration with Knicks fans. As part of AT&T’s Connectivity Partnership, the two New York icons will travel across Manhattan in a taxi, making surprise appearances and giving fans opportunities to win exclusive NBA merchandise, signed memorabilia, and tickets to opening night. “I’m teaming up with Spike Lee, and we’re going to be going to different stores, giving out prizes for AT&T, commemorating the next championship season, and rewarding the fans as well. So I can’t believe that. It seems like we’re still in it, man. You know, everybody’s still excited about the team winning and perhaps maybe repeating, you know, running it back, which hasn’t been done in about eight years. We’ll be coming, celebrating this season throughout the season, the Knicks accomplishment. And after 53 years, the Knicks are finally back on top. Fans can walk in peace and celebrate a championship.” And while the excitement surrounding the Knicks’ championship continues into the new season, perhaps no moment captured the city’s celebration quite like the championship parade itself. As the players celebrated atop their floats and Mitchell Robinson made his way through the streets in his truck, it was only fitting that Clyde, who helped bring New York its first two championships, would lead the celebration through the Canyon of Heroes. But it wasn’t just Clyde’s presence that made the moment special. It was the car he was riding in. Frazier led the parade in the very same 1952 Chrysler Imperial Parade Phaeton that carried the Apollo 11 astronauts through the streets of Manhattan following their historic moon landing in 1969. Now that’s cool! NEW YORK, NEW YORK – JUNE 18: Walt "Clyde" Frazier celebrates during the New York Knicks Championship ticker tape parade and victory rally celebrating winning the 2026 NBA Finals on June 18, 2026 in New York City. The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in five games to win their first NBA Championship in 53 years. (Photo by Roy Rochlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images

stories.title: How long will MPJ be a Net? Does controversy matter?
stories.summary: Here we go again …. and it’s only October.
stories.detailText: MIAMI, FL - OCTOBER 14: Michael Porter Jr. #17 of the Brooklyn Nets moves the ball against the Miami Heat on October 14, 2026 at Kaseya Center in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Eric Espada/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Is Michael Porter Jr. a short-termer in Brooklyn. Brian Windhorst of ESPN thinks so. As he noted on his Hoop Collective podcast Monday: “I would just say that one player to watch this year just in general is Michael Porter Jr. There’s been a lot of attention paid to whether Karl-Anthony Towns got a contract extension which naturally why wouldn’t there be, the man’s a champion. Porter has not gotten a contract extension, he’s in the last year of his contract and he had a pretty good year last year after getting traded there by Denver and you know if a guy’s not in the contract extension you think about you see a possible trade candidate.” Brian Lewis in the New York Post’s season preview thinks so too. As he wrote over the weekend in Nets season preview. “Acquiring Porter (and Denver’s unprotected 2032 first-round pick) for Cam Johnson is a home run deal by any measure. The sweet-shooting small forward led Brooklyn in scoring last season, and could again. But Porter is on a $40.8 million expiring contract and still hasn’t signed an extension since becoming eligible for one on July 6. Is he a building block or asset? If Porter isn’t extended, he’s going to have his name bandied about in trade rumors right up until the Feb. 11 deadline. And if the Nets do move him, is it going to be for future assets? Or do they kick in draft picks of their own for an upgrade?” Neither Porter Jr. nor Sean Marks has expressed any level of panic about an extension. After all, the Nets have until June 30 to proffer him a contract and Marks has spoken about how much he likes Porter Jr. as a player and as an individual. In return, MPJ has continually expressed his desire to stay, praising his young teammates and being the first Net to publicly suggest off-season moves and internal improvements could take the franchise from its third worst win total ever — 20 — to its second highest — 50. As everyone knows, Porter Jr. had his best season ever last year, delivering 24.2 points, 7.1 rebounds and 3.0 assists. On the other hand, he missed 30 games and admitted that after he was snubbed for his first All-Star berth and with all that tanking, he lost interest. Not to mention the steady stream of controversies engendered by his “Curious Mike” podcasts “One thing I regret is that once I didn’t make that All-Star game, I kind of let my foot up off the gas because there was really nothing we were playing for anymore,” Porter said on “Curious Mike” last month. To which Draymond Green responded on “The Draymond Green Show,” his podcast, “You weren’t snubbed! If you finish the rest of that year strong, everybody’s now on the top of their mind coming into the season like, ‘Yo, we got to watch Michael Porter Jr.’ Now, because he didn’t finish the year strong, then people’s just like, ‘Oh man, he’s just out there playing on a bad team to make an All-Star game.’” The implication was that not only did he hurt himself, he hurt his reputation around the league. Indeed, a lot of what MPJ has said on his “Curious Mike” and others’ podcasts has done that. Last season, in fact, the Nets had to take him aside and let him know he’s in New York now and his comments will get magnified, often to the detriment of him and his team. Specifically, the organization was offended , as were many of its fans, by his comments on misogynist Andrew Tate — saying he would “test girls” on “their beliefs” by playing them audio of Tate, whose entire persona revolves around toxic masculinity. Tate is currently fighting extradition from the U.S. to the U.K., where he and his brother face a total of 59 criminal charges, including rape and human trafficking for sexual exploitation. Since then , Porter Jr. said he’s opposed to gay sex but admitted that he “kicked it” with a transsexual woman in Taiwan a couple of years ago adding he didn’t realize she was trans because gender-altering surgeries in Asia ”are so good.” Indeed, Porter’s podcast controversies have become so common that no one in the media (including us) even asked him about it at Media Day. Of course, he’s not required to tow any line or avoid others. His speech is protected as is every American’s and he often takes on subjects that no one else will. The players’ union contract offers more protections. However, as the Tate commentaries attest, your employer is also within his or her rights to condemn you or simply ask that you understand there are boundaries. Most recently , Porter Jr. decided to interview SNEAKO , another in the long list of right-wing social media activists born out of the gaming community. His views have been identified as homophobic, antisemitic, misogynist and violent, getting him banned at one point or another from YouTube, Twitch, TikTok and Instagram. Like his controversial ally, Nick Fuentes, his views on Jews have been deemed particularly hateful. He’s wished Adolf Hitler a happy birthday, said “I’ll be the Nazi and I’ll shove you in the oven like a dirty Jew.” A lot of the criticism of the interview revolved around giving SNEAKO a forum, While much of the interview was a discussion of various conspiracy theories, the presence of demons in American life, the afterlife, Jeffrey Epstein, and other topics popular with his mostly young male audience, there was commentary on the power of the Jewish community. After SNEAKO suggested that Jews as a people have outsized influence throughout the world — a trope used by the Nazis to justify their antisemitic laws and ultimately the Holocaust — Porter responded. “That community specifically, you can call people this name, that name, you can use any slur you want. You start talking about the Jewish community, that’s a completely different animal. That’s the only group you literally cannot say anything derogatory towards. or it can ruin your entire life. your entire image… They band together for sure.” SNEAKO noted at one point that forty percent of NBA owners are Jews. Porter did not endorse SNEAKO’s positions and after the interview criticized him . In the same interview, Porter also expressed frustration about how so many fans at Barclays Center are rooting for other teams, citing the Nets recent preseason game against the Philadelphia 76ers which was LeBron James first appearance in a Sixers uniform. “We just played a preseason game the other night against Philly. You would’ve thought we were in Philly. We gotta get the Brooklyn Nets fans back in there and actually be louder than the opposing team. When we play (New York) Knicks, (Boston) Celtics, Philly, (Los Angeles) Lakers, it’s mostly their fans. It’s crazy,” said Porter. How much of all of this affects negotiations, how much is used by Nets? It’s hard to know and again, free speech matters. But, it’s difficult to imagine how it helps. And how far apart are they on money, on years? Also hard to tell. The final year of his five-year, $170 million deal signed will pay him $40.8 million. Last season, even after the first round of controversy, the Nets didn’t bite on trade packages reportedly offered at the deadline. Then, there’s the key question: what would the Nets want in return? They already have 13 first round picks, second to the OKC Thunder’s 15. Stay tuned. Maybe you’ll find out on “Curious Mike.”

stories.title: NBA has 125 international players on opening day rosters, France leads way with 17
stories.summary: This season, 27.8% of available NBA roster spots are going to international players, down slightly from last season.
stories.detailText: The NBA attracts the top basketball talent from around the globe. As proof, there are 125 international players on NBA rosters to open this season, the league announced. That's 27.8% of the available NBA roster spots going to international players The NBA today announced that opening-night rosters for the 2026-27 season feature 125 international players from a record-tying 43 countries across six continents. All 30 teams feature at least one international player. - 17 players - 16 players - 9 players Dallas,… pic.twitter.com/efEviepb5v — NBA Communications (@NBAPR) October 20, 2026 It's not just the number of players, which is down slightly from last season (135), it's the quality and impact those players have on the league. Four international players have won the last eight NBA MVP Awards: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (2025 and 2026), Nikola Jokić (2024, 2022 and 2021), Joel Embiid (2023) and Giannis Antetokounmpo (2019 and 2020). More than that, last season also was the fifth consecutive year that three international players filled out the top three in MVP voting. Last season it was Gilgeous-Alexander (No. 1), Jokić (No. 2) and Victor Wembanyama (No. 3). More than that, a record 19 international players on opening-night rosters have been NBA All-Stars. At least three international players have made the All-NBA teams every season since 2019. If you're wondering why a lot of people — *raises hand* — believe France as a genuine threat to the USA winning another gold in Men's Basketball at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, consider this: France has a league-high 17 international players on NBA rosters, the most of any country (Canada is next with 16). France can field an entire roster of NBA players, led by Victor Wembanyama, who alone should strike some fear in American hearts. The NBA's representation of players from, or with direct ties to, Africa — a continent where the NBA has worked hard to grow the game of basketball — continues to grow. Including both international and American players, more than 60 players were either born in Africa or have at least one parent born on the continent, a new record. Among those players are seven-time NBA All-Star Joel Embiid (Cameroon), NBA champion and four-time NBA All-Star Pascal Siakam (Cameroon), three-time NBA All-Star Bam Adebayo (ties to Nigeria), Antetokounmpo (parents born in Nigeria), two-time NBA champion OG Anunoby (ties to Nigeria) and 2026 No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa (ties to the Republic of the Congo). NBA opening-night rosters also feature 70 European players, the second consecutive season with at least that many.

stories.detailText: The Washington Wizards will have to wait a little longer before seeing the regular-season debut of their No. 1 pick. Dybantsa will be day-to-day with the injury he suffered in Friday's preseason finale. Keefe termed the injury a mild ankle sprain Friday. stories.summary: The Cavs will be shorthanded in the frontcourt to start the season.
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND, OHIO - JANUARY 04: Nae'qwan Tomlin #35 of the Cleveland Cavaliers drives to the basket against Jaden Ivey #23 of the Detroit Pistons during the second half at Rocket Arena on January 04, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers will be tipping off their season on Thursday against the Philadelphia 76ers without one of their rotation players. The team announced on Tuesday morning that Nae’Qwan Tomlin was “diagnosed with a lower back stress reaction following an evaluation by the Cavaliers medical team.” pic.twitter.com/OS0fXuZyH8 — Cleveland Cavaliers (@cavs) October 20, 2026 Per the Cavaliers’ statement, the team’s medical group identified this injury during an evaluation. Tomlin will be re-evaluated in three to four weeks. I wouldn’t assume that this timeline is definitive, especially with something like this that could vary in severity. It is also fair to note that, with the physical and athletic style of play Tomlin utilizes, the recovery not be as straightforward as other, more standard injuries. Without Tomlin, the Cavs are left with Mario Hezonja and Thomas Bryant as the two established backup bigs. That is far from an ideal group, as Hezonja is still an unknown at this point, while Bryant is a volatile option. This is definitely a missed opportunity for Tomlin to flash. Tomlin hasn’t been able to show much growth in areas of need for his game thus far, and the Cavaliers’ bench feels far from concrete at this point. The start to this season could have been one of the last chances Tomlin had to show he’s deserving of a steady role going forward. With at minimum a month to be missed to start the year, this injury is far from ideal both for Tomlin and the Cavaliers. Last season, Tomlin averaged 5.8 points and 2.9 assists in 64 outings and 15.2 minutes per game.

Here’s the latest from your New York Knickerbockers heading into Ring Night. Enjoy! The challenge is to try to get them enjoy the moment, but not fully. You have to try to supress all that early, before the ceremony, so that you can quickly get not just your body, but your mind and your emotions into the task in front of you.” On how he’ll try to keep the team focused after the ring ceremony: “It’s a challenge. I mean, it’s hard because they’re human, and there’s a part of you that wants to keep celebrating. But you got to turn it off. So the challenge is trying to get them to enjoy the moment, but not fully. I guess, if that makes sense. “Because you have to try to suppress all that early, before the ceremony, during the ceremony, so that you can quickly get, not just your body, but your mind and your emotions into the task in front of you.” On avoiding complacency after winning the NBA championship: “It is a little tough, even for me as a head coach. You have people patting you on the back, telling you how good you are. It’s good, and you want people to be able to do that with you and for you and all that stuff. But in the same breath there always has to be a part of you — and I know this from experience — that says, ‘OK, Don’t listen to this, don’t read this, don’t watch this.’ Because it’s hard to stay even-keeled in situations like that. “You’ve got to embrace it. You’ve got to enjoy it with others, especially your family. But try to come back to earth as soon as possible. And I think our guys have done a good job with it. There have been times when we think we know [what it takes], which is natural, and there’s going to be more times like that during the course of the season. “But at the end of the day, we have a pretty sharp group. And if they don’t know, we’ll definitely help them know that this is not last year. This is a new season and we can’t just think we’re going to switch that light on and get after it.” On James Wiseman facing less pressure with the Knicks than he did with the Warriors: “It was a different situation with the Knicks. You come in as No. 2 pick in the draft with Golden State and you’re talented and skilled as he is and it can be tough on you because of expectations. Not just from the media and fans but sometimes your teammates and coaches and rest of the organization and if it’s hard for certain individuals to live up to. … With this situation, it’s — OK, he’s been around the block, he’s experienced adversity. We’re not looking for him to start or fight for a starting position. We’re not necessarily looking for him to come in and be a backup. He has the luxury of growing at his own pace without much pressure.” Malika: "You're willing to take less (money)?" KAT: "Oh yeah, because I want this team to stay together. That's always been my main priority was to keep everyone here, to keep this core, this special team that we have. So it was the first thing on my mind as soon as it was. And… pic.twitter.com/hU6kaIrwiC — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 20, 2026 Karl-Anthony Towns On his willingness to take a paycut to re-sign with the Knicks: “Oh yeah, (I’m willing to do that), because I want this team to stay together. That’s always been my main priority: to keep everyone here, to keep this core, this special team that we have. So it was the first thing on my mind as soon as it was. And there was nowhere in my mind a max was even thought of.” "Every year is a new year to attack something. When people say we're 'defending the title'…that's one way to look at it. It's something we've won, we've put it in our past, and now we're just trying to attack another." – Jalen Brunson pic.twitter.com/ddURDDVJM4 — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 19, 2026 Jalen Brunson On his message to KAT amid the Knicks contract stalemate: “Sign the contract.” On approaching the new season as a fresh challenge rather than defending a championship: “Every year, it’s a new year to attack something. When people say we’re defending the title — I mean, that’s one way to look at it, but it’s something we won. We’ve put in our past, and now we’re just trying to attack another.” On the importance of retaining the Knicks’ championship-winning core: “[It’s] very valuable. For us to come back, it’s good to have our chemistry continue to grow, understanding that we’ve done it, but are we still hungry, are we still satisfied? Do we continue to get better every single day, or are we just content? That’s our big question that’s going to be answered within the first couple weeks of the season. However we answer it, we’re going to attack it and get better every single day after that.” On wanting to share the Knicks’ championship ring ceremony with the fans: “Definitely special. They deserve it. This is something that’s been brewing for a long time and to share this moment with them is definitely going to be special.” On moving forward after winning the championship: “It’s about how quickly you turn a page and how quickly you understand that the egos have to be checked at the door.” On whether the Knicks have already moved past last season’s championship: “I would say most of, if not all of us, have kind of turned the page already. I think tomorrow is just something we can reflect on and understand what we did. But for the most part, we all turned the page . . . There is no relaxation.” "None of us are satisfied with just this championship. We've got things we're still striving towards. 0-0 starting tomorrow." – Landry Shamet pic.twitter.com/gAsSeqC9gy — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 19, 2026 Landry Shamet On why last season’s championship will no longer matter once the new season begins: “I think the fascinating part about sports is that starting tomorrow, no one cares [about the championship]. After the ceremony’s over, it’s 0-0. We’re a competitive bunch, and by no means is anybody expecting to just coast or anything like that. That’s definitely not the tone of our group.” On the challenge of celebrating a championship and immediately returning to competitive basketball: “I think that’s maybe some of the challenge that I’ve read about and seen in the past that championship teams have. How do you take the high in the celebration at the beginning of the game, and still go out and perform, play the brand of basketball that you’d want to play?” On spending three consecutive seasons with the same NBA organization for the first time: “It’s not lost on me. I feel like I try and do a good job of not taking much for granted. [I’ve] never spent three consecutive training camps with the same organization, so feels really good … to be here and have a familiar group and feel comfortable and confident with the people I’m around. I feel like they feel the same way about me, so I don’t take that for granted at all.” On the Knicks remaining motivated after winning the championship: “I don’t think any of us are ready to sign off and be done playing basketball. We’re all a competitive bunch and by no means is anybody expecting to coast or anything like that. Definitely not the tone of our group.” Hello everyone! stories.title: Who will the Suns face in Portland’s opening night lineup?
stories.summary: Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and Jrue Holiday headline a crowded backcourt as Portland determines its starters against Phoenix.
stories.detailText: Dec 30, 2019; Portland, Oregon, USA; Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard (0) defends Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker (1) during the first half at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-USA TODAY Sports The Phoenix Suns may be benefiting from their opening night’s opponents’ roster construction. When the Portland Trail Blazers, who the Suns play on opening night, signed Damian Lillard in the 2025 offseason, they knew that, barring injuries, they were set for a guard controversy. Rostering NBA champion and defensive guard Jrue Holiday, 2023 third overall pick Scoot Henderson, young scorer Shaedon Sharpe, and Lillard, Portland set themselves up to have a starting guard controversy once the 2026-2027 season rolled around and Lillard recovered from his torn Achilles. Then they traded for Ja Morant this summer, who, despite his recent decline and injury concerns, is another mouth that needs to be fed on offense. Portland’s starting backcourt for opening night is still in question, according to Portland’s head coach, Micah Nori, so which of Portland’s guards are the Phoenix Suns most likely to face in their starting lineup? Let’s take a look at the five and see who the two most likely are. The Unlikely Shaedon Sharpe Off the bat we can eliminate Sharpe, who is expected to be out until at least late February with a torn meniscus. While unfortunate injury news, this comes as a defensive relief for the Suns, who saw Sharpe average 24 points per game on 48% shooting from the field against them last year. Scoot Henderson Henderson finished the 2025-2026 campaign strongly, with multiple 20+ point playoff games against the San Antonio Spurs in the first round of the Western Conference Finals, including a dominant 31-point outing in Game 2 that saw him hit five threes. Being sidelined for most of last season due to a hamstring injury, he played in just 30 games last regular season and started in just a third of them, with nearly all of them coming after Sharpe suffered an injury that kept him out of the starting lineup for the rest of the season, with Henderson taking his place. Eligible for his first contract extension, Henderson and the Blazers have not come to an agreement, a potential sign they want to see him prove himself after an injury-ridden season. Considering the veteran presence on the roster, expect when opening night comes around to see Henderson in a reserve role. The Favorites Jrue Holiday The team’s most consistent point guard last season, after a few down offensive years in Boston taking a back seat to Derrick White, Holiday showed that he can still play the point guard position at a high level, averaging 16 points and six assists per game on 38% shooting from three. Entering the 18th year of his career, he’s started in at least 90% of his team’s games since the 2015-2016 campaign and is known as one of the strongest and best defensive guards in the NBA, helping the Milwaukee Bucks and Boston Celtics win titles in 2021 and 2024, respectively. Holiday didn’t start in the team’s preseason opener, and while he may not be the most dynamic or best scorer out of the five, he’s the best defender, has the most experience in the NBA, and knows what it takes to win at a high level. Suns fans know the type of defender Holiday is better than almost any fanbase… Ja Morant The newest member of the five, the Blazers bought low on Morant this offseason after multiple suspension and injury-riddled seasons since he was an All-Star in 2023. A dynamic scorer and passer, Morant has played more than 60 games over the past five seasons and averaged his lowest points per game since his rookie year, along with the worst shooting percentages from both the field and three, over 20 games last season. While he said he’s open to coming off the bench, he started in the team’s first preseason game, playing just 19 minutes and scoring eight points. Considering his recent rough seasons, three-point struggles, and defensive concerns with his thin frame, Morant is a true wildcard to start. A Surprise if He Didn’t Start Damian Lillard After being traded to the Milwaukee Bucks in 2023 and fully recovered from his torn Achilles, Lillard is set to take back the starting role he once donned in Portland for 11 seasons. An All-Star in the three previous years before he sat out all of last year rehabbing, he’s arguably the greatest Blazer of all time, and the last time he was healthy, he averaged 25 points and seven assists per game. Starting in the preseason opener, like Morant, Lillard is a defensive liability. However, he’s been one of the most productive and high-volume three-point shooters in league history, and considering his leadership, what he means to the organization, and the last time we saw him healthy, he was playing at a high level, at the very least, expect Lillard to be one of the starting guards opening night against the Suns. Most reports have come out signaling that he’s the most likely person to be in the starting lineup out of anyone else in contention. Who do you want to see Portland suit up in the backcourt against Phoenix on opening night?

stories.title: NBA: Timberwolves on NBA GM Survey
stories.summary: Minnesota was voted as one of the best teams in the league, but also one of the most uncertain.
stories.detailText: The NBA General Manager Survey, which consists of 48 questions answered by all 30 NBA general managers, came out this past Thursday and there are many things to react to when you look at the responses with a Timberwolves centric lens. *Keep in mind, GMs could not vote for their own players/team Some of the best in the league The GMs named Anthony Edwards the best shooting guard in the league by a wide margin. Meanwhile they named Jaden McDaniels as a top five perimeter defender, and the team as a whole was tied with the San Antonio Spurs as the team that will be the most fun to watch in the league. What I find most interesting is the fact that there seems to be a clear oxymoron in the way that the GMs voted when regarding the season outlook for the Timberwolves. When asked to rank the teams in the Western Conference, the Wolves were ranked as the clear cut number three team, receiving 53% of the third place votes which was 23 points higher than the next team. What I found odd was the next category. When voters were asked about which team’s success will be the toughest to predict, Minnesota ranked second with 17% of the responses. That doesn’t make a ton of sense to me, as why would they be ranked as the third best team in the west when they’re going to be tough to predict? Most of the questions pertaining to a potential successful season for Minnesota revolve around LaMelo Ball, Jonathan Kuminga, and the bench unit. I understand those uncertainties, but at what point can those just be explained away? The LaMelo Ball mystery LaMelo Ball will play in a true winning environment for the first time in his career, a phenomenon that most pundits don’t know what to do with. I’ll just tell you from my basketball experience, there is a noticeable bump in quality of play when you’re in a winning environment compared to a losing one. It’s easier to make the extra pass, make multiple efforts on defense, or actually attempt to box out when you feel like you have a chance. Look no further than LaMelo’s last year in Charlotte when he was actually surrounded with some talent. They won 40 out of their last 64 games, not including a technical postseason play-in game. No offence to Kon Knueppel or Brandon Miller, but his supporting cast this year will be undoubtedly better. Another concern about LaMelo is his potential fit as a ball dominant guard next to Anthony Edwards, who certainly will have the ball in his hands plenty. To the doubters of that fit with Ant, I want to pose a question to you: What was LaMelo’s first competitive basketball experience? Well, it was being a facilitator for his brothers Lonzo and LiAngelo, of course. I see no reason why he can’t take those skills he learned in his basketball infancy and apply them with his new teammates, most notably Ant and Jaden McDaniels. Kuminga conundrum Let’s now move on to Jonathan Kuminga. I understand the questions. I truly do. I know it didn’t work out in Golden State , and I know his time in Atlanta ended with a whimper. What I also know is that Steve Kerr had it out for him in Golden State, and that Atlanta never really committed to him. At a baseline, he’s a microwave scorer with major athletic upside, shows an affinity to run the floor, and is a big enough body to be able to match up physically. When you look at the other four Timberwolves starters, JK’s archetype is exactly what they need in a four-man. A fourth scorer behind Ant, LaMelo, and Jaden McDaniels, and a capable defender next to Rudy Gobert and Jaden. Kuminga is even a capable shooter, but I don’t worry about that as much. Minnesota will have plenty of shooting in the starting lineup, though it’s nice to know that there is some ability there. There is also some need for scoring with the second unit (more on that later) but JK could easily be appeased with some offensive opportunity when on the floor with the second unit. Depth pieces to prove The last of what could be called one of Minnesota’s main concerns is the quality of the bench guys. Ayo Dosunmu got paid, but behind him there’s not a ton of proven commodities, just some potential. Guys like Joan Beringer, Terrence Shannon Jr., Bones Hyland, and Jaylen Clark all have plenty to prove. But prove what, exactly? Needing someone to spell Rudy Gobert? Even with his fouling problems, Beringer is more than capable of that right now as a rim runner, rebounder, and shot blocker, to say the least. Need some ball handling? Bones Hyland can and will play with the speed this team wants to play at and TSJ can be a menace attacking with his left hand above the break. Jaden is in foul trouble and you need a point of attack defender? As the warden of Clark County Jail, the former college Defensive Player of the Year can handle it, and has shown some shooting improvement in the preseason. We don’t exactly know what we’re going to get from Cody Williams this season, but anything Finch can get from a trade piece that came back from a salary dump is an automatic plus. His shot is a work in progress, but he can defend in rotation and has shown the ability to punch gaps to get to the rim with good ball movement. I’m not saying there aren’t genuine concerns about the Minnesota Timberwolves this season, what I’m saying is that the NBA GMs who voted for the Timberwolves to finish third in the Western Conference are probably more on the nose than those who voted them as the team whose success is most difficult to predict. What do you think? Are the Wolves a clear cut three seed or are they more hard to predict? Sound off in the comments below.

stories.title: Embrace the excitement, Sixers fans
stories.summary: The emotions of this year’s opener are different in a good way.
stories.detailText: While we all know the mental health of every Philadelphia sports fan for at least the next 6-8 months is reliant on the Sixers having a good 2026-27 season, let’s not turn that into a negative. The Sixers are about to open their season at Madison Square Garden against the team that eliminated them from the postseason last spring. The New York Knicks will raise their championship banner on Tuesday night and then it’s all business in a rivalry that might be the juiciest in the NBA during the upcoming season. The emotions of Sixers fans have changed quite a bit from the last time Philly and New York squared off. It was a very bleak Mother’s Day as the Knicks clobbered the Sixers in Game 4 of their Eastern Conference Semifinals series. The goodwill that the Sixers had built up in Philadelphia after rallying from a 3-1 deficit against the Celtics in the first round was quickly gone and the early outlook for the offseason wasn’t particularly optimistic. It felt like the franchise was stuck. We all know what’s happened since. Mike Gansey has given the fanbase a shot in the arm. We won’t rehash the offseason, because that’s also a thing of the past now. The 2026-27 season has arrived. For the first time in a while, instead of waiting for something bad to happen, or even entering the season with a strong sense of apathy, Sixers fans are excited about their team. For some, the players will have to prove they were worth the preseason hype on the court, and that’s fair. But the fact that we’ve reached this point at all, to where the consensus opinion around the Sixers is one of overwhelming excitement, should be a welcomed change. We’re not asking ourselves how many games Joel Embiid is going to miss. We’re not asking ourselves if the rotation is deep enough to withstand problems in the postseason that could come with facing a team with a strong bench like the Knicks. We’re not asking ourselves about possible exit strategies during the season off bad contracts if certain players are to perform well enough to become tradeable. These are all things that Sixers fans have wondered about when new seasons started in recent years. The start of a season was more about how to best weather the inevitable problems that were going to arise instead of simply enjoying the fact that a season was about to start. The start of any season for any sports team at any level is supposed to symbolize hope. Everyone’s starting from scratch and regardless of what the expert pickers are saying about the season, the games will still be played, and the results will be determined by the players between the lines. In recent seasons, Sixers fans understandably have gotten away from those early season feelings of excitement. Fans have become cynical and bracing themselves for pain. Perhaps the 2026-27 will be a new source of disappointment for Sixers fans. But as we prepare to start another Sixers season, there’s certainly more optimism and enthusiasm about the team than there has been in a long time. Enjoy it, Sixers fans, you’ve suffered plenty. You’re allowed to smile for at least a little bit.
