teamStories.detailText: “Rome ne fu[t] pas faite toute en un jour.” I honestly couldn’t tell you how many times I’ve heard that phrase uttered. Not in the original French, of course. But in English, just about everywhere. At work. In casual conversations and in those I’ve overheard. It’s one of those rare gems that you’re as likely to hear in a conference call about a pending contract as when one of your college buddies completes a pyramid of Lone Star tallboys. (Both real examples in my case) Written or spoken, it has infected the parlance like a herpetic strain at a key party — everybody loves to share it. Frankly, I always thought it was kind of redundant. Of course Rome wasn’t built in a day. You’re talking about 1200 years from the founding of the capital city to the fall of the Western Empire. Even long before I could read them, I would stare at Edward Gibbon’s hefty six-volume set on my father’s bookshelves in wonder at the length. Six volumes? For one empire? “And that’s just charting the decline”, my father would invariably answer. Yes, in the end, Gibbon would dedicate over a million words (and most of his life) to the writing and editing of his ‘History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire’ . Spurs fans should be so lucky. And, to be fair, in many ways they have been. Robinson. Duncan. Wemby. It’s a social media narrative now that the Spurs have been blessed beyond both reason and absence of conspiracy. It draws heat like a black hole from a neighboring star, and is no less mythical than still somewhat shrouded origin of the city of Rome, supposedly founded by a pair of men who were nursed by wolves. There are those who believe that Adam Silver bailed out the franchise, and those who refuse to acknowledge the tanking, and those who believe 14% is a reasonable gamble, and those who believe it was destiny. I suppose the rise of an empire always has its murky places — points of debate for historians to engage in years after the music has ended and the chair one might have raced to has long since deteriorated. Still, it’s as hard to deny that the Spurs have felt favored by someone or something as it is that they’ve worked hard for it. I can’t imagine that realms are consolidated any other way. Luck, skill, and effort, they all play their part. Last year the Spurs were lucky until they weren’t. They were skilled until it didn’t matter. They gave effort even when it afforded them no further progress. Now they must evolve. In early October of 105 BC, the bulk of the Roman army found themselves camped on the banks of the Rhône, just outside of Arausio (now known as Orange, France). Approaching the peak of their era in the sun (80ish years from official ’Empire’ status) the Romans had covered themselves in glory, driving out every rival from the Italian Peninsula and defeating the once-mighty Carthage in three successive wars. They’d conquered Macedonia and the whole of Greece, and the constant state of war had hardened their fighting forces to the point of excellence and imbued them with an aura of invincibility. Or so it seemed. Over the past decades, as Rome’s attention was turned elsewhere, a series of Celtic and Germanic tribes had begun to move their way slowly southward, chief amongst them, the Cimbri and the Teutons. Ignored by the Romans, they seemed to pose little threat, until they attacked another Celto-Germanic tribe known as the Taurisci, who happened to live as allies on the northern border of Roman lands. Calling for aid, the Taurisci were certain that the Romans would easily drive away these new enemies. And so were the Romans, until they fought them. Though there’s still some debate over the specific origin of the Teutons, it’s largely agreed that the Cimbri originated on the Danish/German peninsula of Jutland. The shared languages and values necessary for an alliance suggest a similar geographic origin for the Teutons. And why would that matter? Because that’s also where the Vikings came from. The Romans were fighting the (proto) Vikings. And they were not prepared. First the Romans sent some of their legions northward in a show of force, led by Gnaeus Papirius Carbo. Carbo demanded the withdrawal of the tribes, while preparing an ambush irrespective of their compliance. Having agreed to go, the tribes then discovered Carbo’s treachery, and furiously routed him and his army at the Battle of Noreia, all but annihilating the Roman forces (and very nearly killing Carbo). They then turned towards Gaul (Southern France) collecting allies in response to their tales of Roman treachery and defeating the army of Marcus Junius Silanus in the process. The Romans sent another army, helmed by the newly elected Consul Lucius Cassius Longinus and his Legate (Head General) Lucius Caesoninus. After an initial victory at Tolosa, Longinus refused to leave behind the battle spoils to pursue the retreating tribes, who then heavily fortified Burdigala in preparation for battle, and set into motion an ambush of their own. Having finally arrived and fortified the top of a nearby hill, Longinus then opted to split his force and march on the city with only 1/4th of his 40,000 men. Feeling no need to tighten his ranks or march in battle formations, Longinus also refused to send out scouts, and his overconfidence was rewarded with utter defeat and both his and Lucius Caesoninus’ deaths. The 30,000 men on the hill were the only survivors and promptly surrendered, forced not only to give up the aforementioned spoils, but also the majority of their own supplies. Which brings us back to the banks of the Rhône. Now taking the Cimbri, Teutons, and their various allies more seriously, the Romans had dispatched two armies this time. It was a strategy that had worked well for them in both the Samnite and Punic wars, in which pairs of talented generals had worked in tandem to divide, pursue, cut off, and surround their enemies. Many of those generals had been lifelong friends or comrades in arms, though, and the pair who had been selected for this task were decidedly not. Proconsul Quintus Servilius Caepio did not like that a younger, inexperienced candidate had been elected to a consulship over him, and was determined to undermine the admittedly green Gnaeus Mallius Maximus at every opportunity. In the political arena, this would have been all but expected. In the case of open war, however, this was so astonishing a stance that some historians have theorized that the Senior Consul of Rome, Publius Rutilius Rufus, simply failed to consider that Caepio would behave in such a way on the field of battle. And when both armies carved their separate ways to Arausio with relative ease, everything appeared to be going according to the plan. That is, until Caepio refused to cross the river without orders directly from the Senate, refused to combine forces once he’d crossed, and then insisted on continuing to camp separately. As a combined force, the Roman mass was substantial at 80,000 troops and roughly 40,000 auxiliary and support soldiers. Separately, however, they posed less of a threat — and even less than one might think, being unaware of the true size of the combined tribal army opposing them, which numbered close to 200,000 men. Afraid that his young compatriot might try to claim the lion’s share of the glory, the hubristic Caepio attacked the opposing horde without support from Mallius Maximus, and his army was, by all accounts, immediately destroyed, and his camp overrun. Unaware and unprepared for Caepio’s assault, Maximus’ forces watched as 60,000 men at arms were wiped out in front of them. And then the tribes turned their attention to the remaining Roman army. Trapped by the river and having just witnessed the slaughter of their comrades, the remaining Roman forces put up little resistance. The awkward positioning of the inexperienced Maximus’ camp only made things worse, and all told, fewer than 1,000 men survived the day, Caepio and Maximus among them. 120,000 men. The largest Roman force in almost 100 years. Gone. Understandably, for the first time in decades, the Roman populace began to panic. Furor Teutonicus , they called it — ‘Teutonic Fury’, as they awaited invasion in ‘terror cimbricus’ , expecting the Cimbri to appear at the gates of Rome. In a desperate bid, they spontaneously (and in absentia) opted to reelect a previous consul to replace Caepio and Maximus (who were both imprisoned and later exiled), Gaius Marius, hero of the Jugurthine War. And, as in the past, the choice proved to be a wise one. Returning from his campaigns in Africa, Marius studied the circumstances of the recent Roman defeats and decided that the failures had been every bit as structural as strategic. He resolved, in combination with Publius Rutilius Rufus, to pass sweeping military reforms that would help prevent such failures in the future (and would also aid in his effort to build another army from scratch). Left with little more than mercenaries and a few thousand newly-trained legionaries, Marius removed land ownership from the list of requirements for military service, which allowed the landless poor to enlist for the first time, and granted non-citizens a chance at Roman citizenship through a 25-year term of service. He levied for the funds to change the then-seasonal army into a permanent professional force, and improved military training by bringing gladiatorial instructors to train the men how to use their swords. He standardized equipment and had the state supply the army with weapons for the first time, and imposed a code of strict military discipline. He reorganized the standard military unit from irregular ‘maniples’ of 60-120 men into the Roman cohort of 480, demanding that each legionary carry their own rations and heavy equipment to reduce supply lines and the associated issues, allowing each cohort to operate independently and adapt to different combat situations as needed. He even, as the legend goes, personally selected The Aquila , the silver/bronze eagle with a thunderbolt clutched in its talons, as the sole legionary standard. Almost everything you might envision if you were to close your eyes and imagine a typical Roman legion was the result of one of Rome’s greatest and most embarrassing defeats. And all of this took place roughly 500 years after the founding of Rome! The Romans had already conquered and held the whole of Italy. They’d won naval wars and wars abroad. They’d defeated some of their greatest peers and become one of the most imposing powers of their historical era. And they *still* had to refine a bunch of things to become the behemoth that we know them as now. Hopefully, that’s what the Spurs have spent their time doing this off-season. The reality is that these Spurs have lived off the victories and reputations of their predecessors for as long as they realistically could. They were tried and tested by the New York Knicks, and it was revealed that they are not the Spurs of old. They must forge an era all their own. They must refine the process further. They must assess the weaknesses of previous eras and come up with fresh solutions. They’ve made great strides, but now they must become the machine. They like to win with flair and flash, and, as I wrote on several occasions last season, seem to prefer a humiliating victory at the cost of the occasional loss. Now they must learn to love the grind. When Marius reformed the Roman military as he knew it, he abolished the cavalry altogether. And though Caesar Augustus would later reverse that policy in later years, Marius’ message was clear: there will be no cavalry to save you. The legions had to rely on themselves and their training. Every battle would be won or lost, foot by foot, thrust by thrust, from one agonizing end of the battlefield to the other. There would be no fleet-footed horses to bail them out. No stirring charges. Just endless attrition and the smell of leather. Three years later, when the opposing tribes finally moved towards invading Northern Italy, with even more allies in tow, it was barely a contest. In their first serious battle near Aquae Sextiae, 37,000 superbly trained Romans turned back an estimated force of 200,000 Teutons, killing and capturing almost half of that number in a single engagement. The rest of the war went quickly, with the Battle of Vercellae serving as a fitting bookend, as a combined 52,000 Romans crushed the last of the Cimbri to the tune of 120,000+ casualties. This is something these Spurs have in them, too. We’ve seen the havoc they can wreak on an opponent. We’ve seen the speed with which they can bury most teams. But that’s not going to work against the Vikings of NBA contention. There are teams that can match their fury. Wemby’s predecessors set a foundation for an empire to come, but even at their peak, they were labeled “boring” and “robotic”, and they just kept winning. They beat you dribble by dribble, position by position, inch by inch. These Spurs must learn that. Must crave that. Must find their own version of that, in a new era. They’ve patched holes all off-season. They’ve bolstered the ranks with both veterans and youth alike. Their front-court is no longer a question mark. Their backcourt is teeming with talent. Their Superstar is asserting himself early and often. They can turn humiliation into victory. They have the whole season ahead of them to do it. They just have to learn to march in close order. teamStories.detailText: OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA - MAY 30: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs hoist the The Oscar Robertson Trophy with his teammates after defeating the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game Seven of the NBA Western Conference Finals at Paycom Center on May 30, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s finally here! After a shorter-than-we’ve-gotten-used-to offseason thanks to the Spurs making it to the NBA Finals last season, they are back in action and ready for a re-match of the Western Conference Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Last season’s match-up represented a rivalry reborn from 10 years prior, and what a rivalry it is becoming. The two teams now stand a clear tier above the rest of West — which, while still deep, may be falling behind the East in terms of number of contenders — with both teams knowing that anything less than another Conference Finals appearance will be a major disappointment. The question now is, will the chip the Thunder are carrying on their shoulders from the loss to the Spurs in the WCF outweigh the chip the Spurs are carrying from their loss to the Knicks in the Finals, or will their quest for Redemption 2.0 reign supreme? We’ll find out starting tonight! San Antonio Spurs (0-0) vs. Oklahoma City Thunder (0-0) October 20, 2026 | 8:30 PM CT Watch: NBC/Peacock | Listen: WOAI (1200 AM) Spurs Injuries: Tobias Harris — out (calf); Jayden Quaintance — out (knee) Thunder Injuries : Thomas Sorber — out (knee); Nikola Topic — out (back); Otega Oweh — out (Achilles) What to watch for Dynamic Guard Trio Spurs Coach Mitch Johnson said at media day that they would play the guard trio of De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper more than last season, although he couldn’t say how much. Well, he’s throwing them right into the fire as part of the starting line-up on opening night, with Tobias Harris’ calf injury offering the opportunity to experiment a bit. What makes this approach even more interesting is despite losing some size with three guards, Johnson is sticking with Devin Vassell as the fourth starter instead of going back to last year’s starting PF, Julian Champagnie. Of course, this is in line with their preseason approach after Harris was ruled out, and in the final two games when all three guards were available, they faired well, albeit against a Suns team sitting all their starters and a completely inept Kings team. This will be their first real test, and it will be interesting to see how what is a essentially a four-guard lineup does against a much taller Thunder squad, with the 6’5” Vassell matching up against 7’1” Chet Holmgren. Speaking of which… Chet vs. Wemby round bajillion, or is it Mara time? The Thunder will be entering this season with a purpose after the Spurs embarrassed them in the regular season last year, then rallied from a 3-2 deficit to win the Western Conference Finals. Wemby certainly got his revenge on Holmgren for many defeats dating back to childhood, and Chet didn’t seem to want any part of that match-up, as Isaiah Hartenstein mostly covered Wemby unless he and Holgren got switched onto each other. Now, with Vassell at the four, Holgren may find more ways to attack on offense. That being said, OKC is probably hoping it drafted a new future Wemby stopper in Aday Mara: a 7’3”, 255 lb Spanish big man with a 7-6” wing span and reigning NCAA champion and Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year. Of course that is nothing like the Alien’s 8-foot reach, but if Holmgren isn’t up for the challenge, Mara may get thrown into the fire early to see how he matches up. It wouldn’t be fair to expect him to be a Wemby stopper in the first NBA game of his career, and he is expected to be a work-in-progress for a season or two, but it wouldn’t be surprising if Mark Daigneault wants to see what he was right away just for reference. Afterall, similar to the Spurs, the Thunder may eventually have to start considering if they can handle three players on max contracts, and there will be a very heavy burden on Holmgren to prove himself against Wemby this season if he doesn’t want to be the odd man out.

stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- The Rams are signing kicker Brandon McManus , sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday. The Rams worked out McManus and free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday after kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL in a Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals . Grupe was playing in his first game for the Rams after he was signed to replace Harrison Mevis , who missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and then had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of the Rams' Week 5 loss. McManus last kicked for the Green Bay Packers after signing with them in 2024. He was 44 of 51 for Green Bay over two seasons, with six misses coming during the 2025 season. He spent his first nine seasons with the Denver Broncos and one with the Jacksonville Jaguars and was not on a roster to start the 2024 season while being investigated by the NFL for possible violations of the personal conduct policy. In September 2024, the NFL announced McManus was not in violation of the policy and he signed with the Packers three weeks later.

stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Carson Steele #34 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs the ball during an NFL preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five transactions on Tuesday evening. Here’s an overview: RB Carson Steele was waived/injured. RB Jaydon Blue was waived from the roster. C James Brockermeyer and RB Ian Wheeler were released from the practice squad. RB Elijah Mitchell was signed to the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. CARSON STEELE Steele, a preseason fan favorite, recently got called up to the roster after beginning the season on the practice squad. With the Eagles missing their top three running backs due to injury, Steele entered Week 6 as RB2 behind Dameon Pierce. Steele suffered a shoulder injury on his first and only touch of the season, a reception for four yards. He re-entered the game after getting banged up but then left again. Bummer to see him get hurt just as he was getting an opportunity to play. If Steele clears waivers, he will revert to the Eagles’ injured reserve list. JAYDON BLUE The Eagles signed Blue, a fifth-round pick by the Dallas Cowboys in the 2025 NFL Draft, to their practice squad on the last day of August. They then signed him to their roster this past Friday to be a third running back behind Pierce and Steele. But even with Steele getting banged up early on, the Eagles did not trust Blue to play any snaps for them (offense or special teams). Maybe the Eagles will bring him back on the practice squad if he clears waivers. Maybe not. JAMES BROCKERMEYER The Eagles signed Brockermeyer to their practice squad earlier this month, right around when they traded Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens. He was around to provide more center depth. But with Drew Kendall presumably getting healthier, the team apparently deemed Brockermeyer expendable. IAN WHEELER The Eagles signed Wheeler to their practice squad last week to give them more running back depth in practice. But now they’re going with Mitchell, who offers more NFL experience, instead. ELIJAH MITCHELL Mitchell brings experience to the table with 327 career rushing attempts for 1,523 yards (4.7 average) and nine touchdowns. He was previously with the Eagles in training camp before getting hurt. The team placed him on injured reserve and later waived him with an injury settlement. Mitchell is now back in Philly to give the Eagles more running back depth. It’s currently unclear if Saquon Barkley will be ready to return from his hamstring injury in Week 7. If not, Dameon Pierce is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles’ roster with Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley on injured reserve. Depending on Barkley’s status, Mitchell could be temporarily elevated from the practice squad to serve as RB2 or RB3 on Monday night against the Dallas Cowboys.

stories.title: Rams turn to third kicker in three weeks after Blake Grupe's injury
stories.summary: The Rams are turning to their third kicker in as many weeks with Brandon McManus, who takes over after Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams are taking another shot at solving their kicking woes after their fallback plan went awry. The team signed veteran Brandon McManus on Tuesday, Sept. 20. McManus and fellow veteran Matt Prater worked out for the team earlier in the day. The move comes just one day after Rams coach Sean McVay announced that Blake Grupe suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament while trying to make a tackle in the first quarter of an 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Grupe had replaced kicker Harrison Mevis, who added to the team's growing special teams woes when he missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and had a 48-yard kick blocked in overtime of a 37-34 loss to the Buffalo Bills in a Week 5 "Monday Night Football" tilt. The Rams cut Mevis, who made just five of nine field-goal attempts on the season, one day later. McManus, 35, spent the last two years with the Green Bay Packers. His three missed kicks - including an extra-point attempt and field-goal try in the fourth quarter - would loom large in a 31-27 loss to the Chicago Bears in the wild-card round of the NFC playoffs. Despite signing him to a three-year, $15.3 million contract the previous March, Green Bay released the 12-year veteran in May as it prepared to hand the job to sixth-round rookie Trey Smack. McManus becomes the Rams' fifth different kicker since 2023, when Matt Gay left to sign with the Indianapolis Colts. The Rams face the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. stories.detailText: The Rams have found a new kicker. According to multiple reports, veteran Brandon McManus has agreed to join Los Angeles. McManus, 35, was most recently with the Packers last season. He made 24-of-30 field goals and 32-of-33 extra points in 14 regular season games. But in the playoff loss to Chicago, he missed two field goals and an extra point, leading the Packers to move on in the offseason. McManus is a Super Bowl champion, having won it with Denver to cap the 2015 season. He made all 10 field goals and all three extra points in that postseason run. In 186 career regular-season games, McManus has made 82.0 percent of his field goals and 97.4 percent of his extra points. Los Angeles placed kicker Blake Grupe on injured reserve on Monday after he suffered a torn ACL during Sunday’s game against the Cardinals. The club had released Harrison Mevis last week after a rough start to the season. The Rams will be on the road to face the Raiders in Week 7.

stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_siriannionhurts_261020","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"426226","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_siriannionhurts_261020","genre":"News, Trending","guid":"nbc_pft_siriannionhurts_261020","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Philadelphia Eagles","title": "What to make of Sirianni’s comments on Hurts","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/what-to-make-of-nick-siriannis-comments-on-jalen-hurts-situation","availableDate":"2026-10-20T12:50:30Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} To no surprise, the NFL won't be taking any action against the Eagles for its handling of the Jalen Hurts blood clot prior to Hurts playing in Week 5. While the league has yet to issue a statement to that effect (or to make anyone available for questioning by reporters on the issue), an unnamed source told Jonathan Jones of The Athletic that the NFL has concluded the situation " was handled appropriately " by the team. It's not a surprise because the Eagles have said , and the league has confirmed , that the team "remained in communication" with the NFL throughout the process. That's the best way to avoid league scrutiny; the Eagles involved the league in the various decisions that were made. Jones also reports that Dr. Allen Sills, the NFL’s chief medical officer, worked with the Premier League's chief medical officer to have Hurts evaluated at the Cleveland Clinic in London on the evening of Saturday, October 10. The unnamed source told Jones that the team, the staff, the doctors, and Hurts determined he could play the next day against the Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Jones also reiterates the claim, which surfaced after multiple reports claimed Hurts was advised not to sleep , that Hurts "returned to the team hotel around 2:45 a.m. local time Sunday and slept until about 10 a.m.," and that he "took a nap" at the stadium before the game. The unnamed source also repeats (as the NFL told PFT last week ) that the team did not violate the injury reporting rules by, for example, failing to downgrade Hurts to "questionable" the moment his availability was, you know, in question or by failing to disclose that his "calf" injury was in reality a blood clot. Again, the league's position isn't a surprise. The NFL and the Eagles were and are in lockstep on this issue, which based on the evidence that has been disclosed to date calls into question a lingering cultural reality that healthcare for players seems to be more about checking the boxes required to allow a player to " be available " to play and less about treating the player like any patient who would show up with a problem that requires diagnosis, treatment, and recommended steps to ensure a full and successful return to health, with all other considerations taking a back seat. Much more should be demanded of the league and its teams on issues like this. So far, however, the NFL Players Association has been conspicuously silent. Many details remain unavailable. Reports from established "insiders" have painted a picture that has been confusing at times, downright bizarre at others. From the question of whether the league and its teams are truly providing meaningful healthcare to player-patients to the question of whether the league and its teams are creating even more inside information that could be misused for betting purposes (while the millions who are constantly bombarded with gambling ads are kept in the dark regarding the truth as to a player's health), the Hurts case raises very real questions that, with the passing of time, the playing of more regular-season games, and the inevitable emergence of the next story that attracts the media's attention, will fade away and never be adequately answered.

stories.title: Rams sign another new kicker
stories.summary: Brandon McManus is the third official kicker of the season and it’s not Week 7 yet
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams’ third kicker of this season is veteran free agent Brandon McManus. Technically, McManus will be the fourth because punter Ethan Evans kicked a PAT last week after Blake Grupe tore his ACL, but in any case the Rams continue to cycle through kickers like most people go through Brita filters. McManus is signing with the L.A. Rams immediately after he beat out Matt Prater in an audition for the job on Tuesday. He is set to be the Rams’ kicker against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The #Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus, per me and @MikeGarafolo , the latest in Los Angeles’ kicker saga. He worked out today, along with FA K Matt Prater. McManus most recently kicked for the #Packers and #Broncos . pic.twitter.com/eyzO9QmQjt — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 20, 2026 This will officially be the 13th season of McManus’s career. An undrafted free agent out of Temple in 2014, McManus spent his first nine years with the Denver Broncos, and he made 81.4% of his field goal attempts. He kicked for the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2023, then the Green Bay Packers in 2024 and 2025. He was 20-of-21 over 11 games with Green Bay last season. McManus immediately replaces Grupe and the recently-released Harrison Mevis. If he fails or gets injured, it looks like Prater could be the next man up and fans shouldn’t put it past L.A. to continue making moves at kicker this season. The only question is, when will this madness be settled with a real kicker?

stories.title: Jim Nantz says he 'learned a lesson' trying to Peanut punch ball from J.J. Watt: Don't do it
stories.summary: Jim Nantz took J.J. Watt's invitation to demonstrate the Peanut punch while they were broadcasting Sunday's Bills-Raiders game — "and as soon as I did it, I regretted it," he told Pat McAfee.
stories.detailText: Former NFL player J.J. Watt, shown talking with his present- day broadcast booth partner Jim Nantz, at the 2025 Masters tournament in Augusta, Ga. (Ashley Landis / Associated Press) Jim Nantz is fine. The 67-year-old sportscaster didn’t actually injure himself demonstrating the so-called “Peanut” punch with CBS broadcast booth partner J.J. Watt — who is 37 and a three-time former NFL defensive player of the year — during the Buffalo Bills-Las Vegas Raiders game on Sunday. He seems to feel foolish though. “I learned a lesson,” Nantz said Tuesday on ESPN’s “ The Pat McAfee Show .” “You got J.J. Watt cradling the ball like this. What am I — I’m going to like knock it out of his hands? Come on, the thing was vacuum sealed into his chest.” Read more: U2 will headline halftime show for Packers-Rams Thanksgiving eve game on Netflix Named after retired cornerback Charles “Peanut” Tillman , the “Peanut punch” has become an effective method for defensive players to cause fumbles. While showing viewers how offensive players should hold the football to counter the maneuver , Watt encouraged Nantz to “give that a good punch.” “Really?” Nantz asked. JIM NANTZ JUST TRIED TO PEANUT PUNCH @JJWatt 🤣 "I did not think you were gonna go that hard" "my wrist is broken" 😭 pic.twitter.com/ocdRBn282r — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 “Hard as you got, brother,” Watt replied. So Nantz delivered a solid blow to the ball, which didn’t budge in Watt’s arms. “I did kind of go aggressively here after this ball because J.J. encouraged me to do so,” Nantz told McAfee while watching a clip of the incident. Back on the broadcast, Nantz immediately winced and grabbed his hand. Read more: ESPN's Troy Aikman says he'll be 'free agent' after season, laughs at reported tension with Joe Buck “I did not think you were going to go that hard,” Watt laughed. “That was so much harder than I thought you were going to go.” Nantz clearly was in discomfort, but he chuckled about it as well. “My wrist is broken,” he told his booth partner. “Like I’m going to knock it out of your hands.” “Get Jim some ice,” Watt joked as they were going to commercial. Read more: Tony Romo and CBS Sports have 'mutually agreed to part ways' following his OWI arrest After halftime, Nantz could be seen in the booth with his hand wrapped . That led some people to believe he had seriously injured himself. “I heard from people you can’t believe,” Nantz told McAfee. “[Bills quarterback] Josh Allen texted me an hour after the game and said, ‘Did you just break your hand? I hear you broke your hand.’ I heard from a former president of the United States, reached out and wanted to know if my hand was broken.” McAfee and company speculated that the former president was Barack Obama , but Nantz did not reveal his identity. After the game, Watt joked on X : “CBS Injury Report Week 7 — Jim Nantz: Questionable (Wrist/Hand).” Read more: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season after blood clots found in lungs The NFL joined in the good-natured fun, posting the clip on Instagram and writing, “the peanut punch isn’t for everybody,” along with a laughing emoji. While Nantz admitted his hand and wrist “did hurt for a while,” he told McAfee that any reports beyond that were “greatly exaggerated.” “It did sting, I’m not going to kid you,” Nantz said. “But I gave it my best, and as soon as I did it, I regretted it because I felt like everything had been compressed. And I did think I was going to wake up Monday with this thing about triple the size, but I’m fine. I’m not going to be on the injury report this week. I’m going to be good to go. No broken bones.” Get the best, most interesting and strangest stories of the day from the L.A. sports scene and beyond from our newsletter The Sports Report. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: NFL to increase security in Paris for Steelers-Saints game
stories.summary: The NFL said security will be heightened for the game in Paris between the Steelers and Saints after civil unrest engulfed the French capital last weekend.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK -- The NFL said security will be heightened for the game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints on Sunday after civil unrest engulfed the French capital last weekend. Executive VP of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly said officials are collaborating with Parisian and national authorities overseas, along with the U.S. State Department. League officials, including senior VP of security Cathy Lanier, have been on the ground in France, according to O'Reilly. "There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security -- everybody involved with this game," O'Reilly said at the league's annual fall owners meeting. "Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams." O'Reilly said there was never a point that the game was in danger of not being played at Stade de France, which is in the outskirts of Paris in Saint-Denis. He cited other sporting events ongoing in the city, including a Champions League soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona on Tuesday night. The NFL has in the past moved games to avoid getting in the way of local response to an unforeseen event, and officials believe that is not an issue for the league's debut in France. "We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," O'Reilly said. "That's always top of mind for us, and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game." Rioters clashed with police, set cars on fire, stormed public buildings and engulfed a historic city hall in flames in France's worst civil unrest in years as violence and looting swept through major cities. About 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend, and authorities said thousands of businesses were damaged or looted. The rioting overshadowed demonstrations against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools in which hundreds of thousands of people marched peacefully. The Saints traveled directly to Paris after playing at the New York Giants and are practicing in the area this week. The Steelers are set to travel closer to kickoff. With the collective bargaining agreement allowing for up to 10 international games, O'Reilly said that number is being considered for next season. There are a record nine on the schedule this year. Where those games take place is still being discussed. "We like continuity, but we are looking at new regions, and Asia would be one of them," O'Reilly said. After so much talk leading up to and coming out of the game in Melbourne, Australia, about the Los Angeles Rams waiting until late to fly there -- and lost 27-7 to San Francisco -- the NFL does not appear close to dictating when teams must travel. "That is the discretion of the club," O'Reilly said. "As it stands today, you let the football decisions reside at the football level in terms of how they want to plan and prepare for a game coming in. That's not something we're ruling out, and there could be discussion on is there some standardization in the future. But right now, that's the prerogative." With his suspension over Tuesday, 49ers owner Jed York was in attendance for the fall meeting. York was suspended for six games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy after being arrested in a prostitution sting in Ohio in August. He pleaded no contest to two misdemeanors but was still punished by the league and stayed away from the 49ers during their 6-0 start. York didn't attend the owners' meetings in Atlanta the week of his arrest.

stories.title: Amid civil unrest in Paris, NFL has 'never been close' to moving first game in France
stories.summary: NFL officials have been in Paris for about 10 days working on logistics, league exec Peter O'Reilly said. "We've got confidence in the plans, both from an ops and a security standpoint."
stories.detailText: NEW YORK — The NFL's first game in France is scheduled for Sunday between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints. The game is expected to continue as scheduled despite unrest in Paris and across France. About 2,400 people were arrested nationwide over the weekend amid riots over living costs and poor conditions in schools, per the Associated Press . "All of our plans for the Paris game this weekend are moving forward as planned," said Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president of club business, international and league events, on Tuesday from league meetings. "We're obviously working and collaborating very closely with the Parisian French authorities, as well as the State Department. Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams. … "We've got confidence in the plans, both from an ops and a security standpoint." NFL officials have been in Paris for about 10 days working on logistics, O'Reilly said. Among those on the ground is NFL senior vice president of security Cathy Lanier, who previously served as the Chief of Police for the Washington D.C. Metropolitan Police Department. NFL EVP Peter O’Reilly on Steelers-Saints playing in Paris this weekend amid unrest: All of our plans in Paris are moving forward. We’re confident in our operational and security plans… being very vigilant in everything we do and all of our planning. pic.twitter.com/UseKPWFs3U — Jori Epstein (@JoriEpstein) October 20, 2026 Stade de France, where the game will be staged, has hosted major international games before, including the 2024 Paris Olympics. The Saints flew from New York to Paris on Sunday night after beating the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. The Steelers are scheduled to fly to Paris on Thursday. "All of our events we have going on, we always have a very strong security presence around all of those events," O'Reilly said. "And that presence will be heightened with local authorities making sure that there's nothing more important from our standpoint than the team security, the fan security, everybody involved with this game. So, extremely vigilant, as we always are. As I said, confident in all of those plans as we head towards Sunday." The NFL has previously considered relocating domestic games when natural disasters, such as wildfires in Southern California, have dictated that resources not be redirected to a football game. O'Reilly said that is not a concern for the league with the game and surrounding fan events. "We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," O'Reilly said. "That's always top of mind for us and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game." The Saints improved to 2-4 with their 34-27 win over the Giants. The Steelers arrive at 4-2 after a 26-19 overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. France marks the third new market this season for the NFL, which played in Melbourne, Australia and Rio de Janeiro, Brazil this fall after two seasons playing in São Paolo. The NFL has nine total international games this season across Melbourne, Rio de Janeiro, London, Paris, Madrid, Munich and Mexico City. O'Reilly said the league is considering expanding to 10 international games next year, which is the maximum amount allowed by the league's current collective bargaining agreement with the NFL Players Association. The NFL continues to have interest in playing a game in Asia, and particularly Japan, but has not finalized plans to announce a game there yet. Some countries that hosted games this year are likely to win bids for 2027, including some games in new cities for returning countries akin to the NFL's recent model in Brazil. Has the NFL considered moving the game out of Paris due to unrest? "We have never been close to that point," O'Reilly said. "We've always got contingency plans for every game, every single one of them. But no, we were not at that point at any point in the conversation."

stories.title: Caleb Williams has gone from 32nd last year to first this year in completion percentage
stories.summary: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is a different player in 2026.
stories.detailText: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is a different player in 2026. In 2025, Williams finished the season ranked 32nd in the NFL with a completion percentage of 58.1 percent. This year, Williams ranks first in the NFL with a completion percentage of 72.5 percent. On Sunday against the Falcons, Williams completed 30 of 36 passes, a completion percentage of 83.3 percent. That was the best mark of his career. Williams is throwing the ball more accurately than ever. When Ben Johnson became the Bears' head coach last year, one of his stated goals was for Williams to have a completion percentage of at least 70 percent. Even as the Bears and Williams improved significantly in Johnson's first year, Williams' completion percentage stayed low. But during training camp this season, Johnson sounded confident that Williams' completion percentage was going to keep trending upward . Johnson couldn't have been more right about that. Williams is throwing the ball more accurately than any quarterback in the NFL.

stories.title: Falcons release LB Bralen Trice
stories.summary: With word emerging earlier on Tuesday that the Falcons were adding linebacker Charles Snowden, Atlanta has opened a roster spot.
stories.detailText: With word emerging earlier on Tuesday that the Falcons were adding linebacker Charles Snowden, Atlanta has opened a roster spot. The Falcons announced the club has released linebacker Bralen Trice. Trice was just added to the 53-man roster over the weekend from the practice squad. The 2024 third-round pick has appeared in four games this season — the first four of his career. He’s registered two total tackles and one pass defensed in 76 defensive snaps and five special teams snaps. Atlanta also announced the club has signed linebacker TJ Quinn to its practice squad.

stories.title: Cowboys sign QB Kyle Trask to their practice squad
stories.summary: The Cowboys needed a third quarterback after losing Joe Milton off their practice squad.
stories.detailText: The Cowboys needed a third quarterback after losing Joe Milton off their practice squad. Milton signed with the Eagles this week after Philadelphia starter Jalen Hurts was lost for the season. Dallas signed quarterback Kyle Trask to the practice squad, the team announced Tuesday. He joins Dak Prescott and Sam Howell at the position. Trask spent training camp with the Panthers, but has remained a free agent since they cut him Aug. 30. He entered the NFL as a second-round pick of the Buccaneers in 2021. Trask appeared in seven games with the Bucs, playing 32 total snaps. He is 4-of-11 for 28 yards. He was briefly on the Falcons' practice squad last season. The Cowboys also announced they signed safety Juanyeh Thomas to the active roster from the practice squad. In a corresponding move, they waived cornerback Caelen Carson.

stories.title: Texas isn’t translating practice into games
stories.summary: Justin Cryer believes that the players have to take accountability for their mistakes because the coaches are putting them in positions to succeed.
stories.detailText: AUSTIN, TX - OCTOBER 17: Florida Gators tight end Lacota Dippre #17 catches a touchdown pass while being defended by Texas Longhorns linebacker Justin Cryer #28 during the SEC football game between the Texas Longhorns and Florida Gators on October 17, 2026, at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images AUSTIN — As momentum swung in favor of the Florida Gators after a late touchdown in the first half , head coach Jon Sumrall’s team mounted a grinding, 15-play, 69-yard touchdown drive that took 8:03 off the clock and tied the game at 17-17, keeping the Texas Longhorns offense off the field for half the third quarter. The Texas defense had held Florida without a third-down conversion in the first half, but the Gators converted five straight third downs on their lengthy drive, but none was more frustrating than the final conversion, a 3rd and 3 from the 8-yard line that resulted in an eight-yard touchdown catch by tight end Lacota Dippre, his second of the game. Tramell Jones Jr. leads Florida down the field on an 8 MINUTE drive and finds Lacota Dippre for the touchdown. Tie game in Austin 🐊👀 pic.twitter.com/BkkjjZljLQ — CFB Kings (@CFBKings) October 17, 2026 The most frustrating element of the touchdown? Texas was well prepared for the play, a mesh concept with Dippre simply running up the seam after both tight ends shifted from the field to the boundary and the boundary wide receiver motioned across the field, because the Longhorns had practiced it four times before the game, Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Monday. “All of a sudden it comes in the game and we’ve got three guys guarding a running back and nobody guarding a tight end over the middle of the field,” Sarkisian said. Senior linebacker Justin Cryer was the player responsible for the running back as senior safety Jelani McDonald and sophomore nickel back Graceson Littleton both blew their assignments, leaving the other tight end open in addition to Dippre. The breakdown left Cryer visibly upset on the field after the inexplicable busts by a team leader who has played more than 1,500 career snaps in McDonald and a player in Littleton who has been reliable since he arrived on campus and immediately earned a starting role at an extremely demanding position. “We’ve practiced this not even 24 hours ago, right?” Cryer said Monday. “So for us to go out there and mess that up, it’s like, man, we have to just have better focus in in the moment, right?” The Florida State transfer believes the players have to take responsibility for those mistakes, which were not limited to that play defensively or even to that unit, because the coaches put the players in position to have success. “I can count countless plays up that we practiced and we’ve gone over and we did not do a good job,” Cryer said. “So again, taking ownership of that, right? They’ve put us in the best position to go out there and do it. As players, we have to do a better job, and there’s no other way to put it.” The persistent problems put the coaches in a difficult position — if players are making mistakes in practice, the coaches can work to fix those problems before games or remove offensive calls from the game plan if they aren’t working practice, but making those mistakes in games after practicing well changes games. Sarkisian saw the same issues offensively, particularly in the run game, which found some rare explosive runs in a 31-yard effort by senior running back Hollywood Smothers and a 21-yard touchdown run by fifth-year Raleek Brown, but as the game went on, there were too many breakdowns as the Longhorns had six runs stuffed and 12-of-25 runs go for two yards or less . “It’s hard to point out specific runs to you guys, but we’re calling specific runs, and we’re not blocking them the way that we practice those exact plays in practice during the week,” Sarkisian said. The issues extend to special teams — Sarkisian wasn’t specific about any special teams mistakes on Saturday, when Texas struggled with short kickoffs and poor coverage that resulted in five returns for 105 yards, including a long of 30 yards, but the punt down the middle of the field against Tennessee returned for a touchdown and the simulated fair catch by punt returner Ryan Niblett that negated a significant return by Jermaine Bishop stand out, not to mention the blocked punt by Oklahoma that turned into a touchdown on a basic protection breakdown. “We have to do a better job taking practice to the game and having a sense of belief and confidence that what you’re doing is the right thing to do,” Sarkisian said. The Longhorns also have to avoid pressing to make plays instead of relying on their technique and fundamentals. “When there’s a standard and expectation of performance, sometimes we can try too hard, and we can start chasing plays as opposed to just executing the play that you have,” Sarkisian said. “So I think we need to settle down a little bit offensively and just execute the play and let the flow of the game happen. Do it at a high level, but just execute the play. We don’t need to chase the play.”

stories.title: Reports: NFL won't punish Eagles for letting Jalen Hurts play with blood clot
stories.summary: The NFL will not punish the Eagles for how they handled the process surrounding quarterback Jalen Hurts being cleared to play Week 5 against the Jaguars, according to multiple reports.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- The NFL will not punish the Philadelphia Eagles for how they handled the process surrounding quarterback Jalen Hurts being cleared to play Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars , according to multiple reports. The league's decision was first reported Tuesday by The Athletic, which also reported that the NFL determined the Eagles did not violate the league's injury report policy. Hurts, 28, is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday. In a statement released Tuesday, the NFL said officials had been in contact with Eagles medical personnel and Cleveland Clinic London throughout the process of Hurts being treated. "The league's Chief Medical Officer, Dr. Allen Sills, arranges for medical resources with leading providers in every international market with approval from the NFL Players Association," the league said. "Medical care for players is provided by club medical staff in coordination with independent doctors." Sills and other officials are expected to address reporters at the league's annual fall meeting later Tuesday in New York. Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for at least three months, sources informed of the diagnosis told Rapoport and Schefter. Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs. Hurts was initially diagnosed with what was described as a superficial blood clot in his calf. That diagnosis occurred in London before the Eagles' Week 5 game against the Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Hurts played in that game -- a 19-17 loss for the Eagles -- despite the initial diagnosis and attempted 40 passes. Sources told Rapoport that Hurts was in the hospital late at night in London and upon returning to the hotel at 3 a.m. local time, he was able to sleep until the team left for the stadium at 10:30 a.m. Upon arrival, Hurts napped until heading out to the field for pregame warmups. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni did not go into detail about why Hurts was allowed to play in the Jaguars game after he was diagnosed with a blood clot but maintained that "the health of our players is always at the forefront of our mind" while expressing "full faith" in the team's medical experts. "The same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys, to help them," Sirianni said Monday. Hurts' clot is considered to be "provoked" -- meaning a favorable prognosis with treatment and care -- because he was cleated in his calf, sources told Rapoport. The Eagles placed Hurts on injured reserve three days ago after consultations with numerous doctors and experts. Hurts already had been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers , but the Eagles waited to make the roster move until after consulting with medical experts. Sirianni would not reveal the contents of his personal conversations with Hurts but acknowledged that not having Hurts on the field for the foreseeable future will mean a transition. "I haven't been without Jalen for an extended period of time," the coach said. "I have the utmost confidence in Tanner, but I miss him. I miss him, and I know that will be the case because Jalen and I have been together, head coach and quarterback, for six years, so that's natural." "I don't want to speak for him in any sense of the matter, but I deeply care about him and hope that he continues to improve with what he's going through." Hurts took a cleat to his calf area Oct. 4 against the Los Angeles Rams . He informed the Eagles' medical staff of the injury after practice Oct. 8 and was back at practice the next day before the team left for London. An ultrasound in London on Oct. 10 revealed Hurts' superficial blood clot. The Eagles said last week that their medical staff and London-based doctors reviewed the ultrasound results and "concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play" against the Jaguars. After returning to Philadelphia, Hurts underwent a follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday that revealed movement in the blood clot, prompting the Eagles to rule him out for the game against the Panthers. Hurts hadn't missed more than two games in a season since becoming Philadelphia's quarterback in 2021. He is the fourth-leading passer in franchise history and has led the Eagles to three NFC East titles, two Super Bowl appearances and a victory over the Kansas City Chiefs two years ago in Super Bowl LIX, when he was named MVP. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.title: Steelers Week 7 power rankings roundup: Starting to believe yet?
stories.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers Week 7 power rankings roundup.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers needed overtime to complete a comeback victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road. Timely fourth-quarter interceptions by Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette helped the Steelers take the lead late, while Germie Bernard scored the game-winning touchdown in overtime. As always, let’s have a look around the internet to see where other media outlets have the Steelers ranked among the rest of the NFL in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No.15 (No. 17 Last Week) “I feel like I say this every week, but this is the most confusing team in the league for me. The Steelers look great, then they look terrible, and sometimes — like in their 26-19 overtime in Tampa on Sunday against the Baker Mayfield-less Bucs — they alternate between great and terrible within the same game. They were terrible for three quarters and trailed 16-3. But their defense kept them in it. Then Aaron Rodgers woke up a little. Then he went off in overtime (6 for 7, 51 yards and a TD). I don’t know. They’re 4-2, but the roller coaster is making me a little nauseous.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.16 (Last Week No.16) “The people who bet on Dowdle this season are not happy. The veteran running back was taken off the board 73rd on average, but he’s 215th in scoring (6.1) after Jaylen Warren has taken firm hold of the top spot in Pittsburgh. Warren is 42nd in fantasy scoring (17.1), the highest spot for any Steeler.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.17 (Last Week No. 13) “At 4-2, they are tied atop the AFC North. But do we really know how good or bad they are? The defense showed up against the Bucs.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.13 (Last Week No. 12) “Time to get Le Torchon Terrible ready.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.17 (Last Week No.22) “It took them nearly all afternoon, but the Steelers finally did it: They found enough offensive production to win a game in an even-numbered week. An unrelenting fourth-quarter comeback effort saw Pittsburgh steadily chip away at Tampa Bay’s lead, taking its own lead late in regulation before asserting dominance in overtime with a 12-play, 70-yard touchdown drive that ended in a Germie Bernard touchdown catch from 6 yards out. The triumphant finish followed a frustrating first three quarters that were all too familiar to Steelers fans, but their ability to break free from their struggles suggests they might have finally unlocked what seemed buried in prior weeks — or at the very least, finally learned how to adjust in game enough to produce late-stage progress. Aaron Rodgers’ reliance on the quick passing game sparked the offense, and Bernard turned in his best rookie performance yet in a Pittsburgh win without significant output from Jaylen Warren. Perhaps these Steelers have some versatility after all.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.16 (Last Week No. 17) “Are the Steelers doing it again? Nothing about them is impressive … except their record. That’s a recurring theme for the Steelers in recent seasons. Pittsburgh trailed 16-3 through three quarters on Sunday and came all the way back to win in overtime. They won despite not having a play longer than 19 yards. They averaged 3.9 yards per play.” “Aaron Rodgers’ performance summed up the day, and the Steelers’ start as well. Against Tampa Bay, he had a negative EPA per play and a very low 3.91-yard average depth of target, according to Sumer Sports. Somehow the Steelers got the win. And they’re two games over .500 with Rodgers being below average across the board in his age-42 season.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.18 (Last Week No.17) “He’s only had the benefit of two starts, but WR Germie Bernard already ranks second among all rookies with 24 receptions (17 in those two starts, including 11 in Sunday’s win at Tampa.)” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.17 (Last Week No. 20) “The Steelers’ offensive consistency issues center on third-down inefficiency. They’ve converted only 33% of their attempts, fifth worst in the league. The passing game has struggled against man coverage on third down, and coach Mike McCarthy has acknowledged it, saying he “definitely wants to get the ball ran more.” Even in Sunday’s overtime win over the Bucs, the Steelers went 5-of-15 on third down, including a failed third-and-goal pass to DK Metcalf from the 1 late in the fourth quarter that helped give Tampa Bay enough time to force overtime.” – Cameron Wolfe While I was a bit shocked to see the Steelers fall in a few outlets’ rankings, I suppose it makes sense given the way the Steelers won. Pittsburgh looked lifeless on offense for three quarters before they picked things up with the help of turnovers. The Steelers have obvious problems on both sides of the ball, but keep finding ways to win games. Pittsburgh is the early favorite in Week 7, as they travel to Paris to take on the New Orleans Saints. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_jedyork_261020","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"381314","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_jedyork_261020","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pft_jedyork_261020","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"San Francisco 49ers","title": "Will 49ers make a big move with York back?","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/will-49ers-make-a-big-move-with-jed-york-back-from-suspension","availableDate":"2026-10-20T12:40:05Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} On the same day his six-game suspension following an August arrest in Ohio ended, 49ers owner Jed York was present at the quarterly gathering of the most exclusive club in American sports. Via multiple reports, York is attending the 2026 fall meetings in New York. York quickly pleaded no contest to a pair of misdemeanors after he was arrested in a prostitution sting operation in East Palestine, Ohio. He had arranged a meeting with a fake sex worker, and he was apprehended while looking for a fictitious lot at a trailer park. He voluntarily skipped three games. Earlier this month, the NFL suspended York for six games, giving him credit for the three games in which he self-suspended. The league also fined York $500,000. As mentioned earlier today and on PFT Live , the NFL has a lingering disparity regarding the financial consequences of player and owner suspensions . Players, when suspended, lose 100 percent of their compensation. They also become potentially responsible to repay portions of previously-paid signing bonuses or roster bonuses. Owners lose none of their NFL income; they simply pay a separate fine. And that won't change, because the league is the owners. Changing the suspension formula to match the impact of player suspensions would be the equivalent of Congress voting to enact term limits or any other bill that would directly impact them in a potentially negative way. It also won't change because there's no public push to change it. There's no public push for it to change because few in the media make the point that the system creates a dramatic difference between the impact of a suspension on a player's earnings and an owner's.

stories.title: Ravens re-sign K Jake Moody after another Tyler Loop miss in Cleveland
stories.summary: The Ravens are (again) bringing in kicking competition for Tyler Loop after another miss against the Browns on Sunday.
stories.detailText: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Jake Moody #16 of the Washington Commanders attempts a field goal against the Philadelphia Eagles in the first quarter at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update, 4:00 p.m. ET: The Ravens also waived linebacker Carl Jones Jr. from the 53-man roster. He will likely re-sign to the practice squad on Wednesday with two elevations remaining for the rest of the season. The Baltimore Ravens re-signed Jake Moody to the practice squad on Tuesday, according to the NFL’s daily transaction notice, once again adding competition for kicker Tyler Loop after two misses inside 50 yards in the last three weeks. Moody, 26, first signed in Baltimore on September 1 following Loop’s uneven preseason. But the second-year kicker went seven-for-seven on his kicks in Week 1, including a career-long 57-yard field goal, reviving team confidence and leading to Moody’s release a few days later. Loop continued to perform to start his sophomore campaign. A 49-yard attempt was blocked in Week 2, but he hit all six of his kicks in Rio, including a 56-yard game-winner, the first of his career, to cap off the Ravens’ seven-second miracle. The 25-year-old then crushed a 64-yard field goal in Week 4 that overshadowed a bad miss from 40 yards that seeemed to be an operational issue. Loop knew the assignment in Atlanta in Week 5 with Lamar Jackson sidelined. He nailed two field goals from 50-plus, bringing him to five-for-five on such kicks for the year. But in Cleveland on Sunday, he pulled a fourth-quarter 49-yard attempt wide left, and the Ravens lost by three points. Loop’s 76.9% field goal conversion rate is now well behind his 88.2% mark as a rookie. His success from long-distance has been remarkable after last season’s one-of-four showing, but three misses inside of 40 yards is unacceptable. The 2025 sixth-round pick obviously has the leg for the NFL, but his inconsistency is maddening. Moody has dealt with his share of struggles since entering the league in 2023 as a 49ers third-round pick. He was relatively reliable as a rookie, but his play fell off a cliff in 2024, though a whopping 20 of his 34 attempts came from 40 yards or longer. Last year, he made 19 of his 23 attempts while playing for three different teams. Notably, he went 10-for-11 in Washington to close out the year but could not beat out a rookie for the Commanders’ kicking job in training camp. It would likely take a calamitous Week 7 showing from Loop to motivate the Ravens to make a change, but if misses keep stacking over the next few weeks, Jesse Minter may have no choice but to give Moody a shot.

The Buffalo Bills’ bye week is upon us, and there’s plenty to discuss in the absence of a game this coming weekend. The offense is also currently ranked first in pass yards per play, and second in yards per play, as well pass yards per play. It’s Buffalo’s defense that could stand to improve, currently ranked 28th in points given up per game, plus 31st in both yards given up per game and pass yards given up per game.
