stories.title: Caleb Lomu’s versatility comes into focus after Patriots O-line injuries
stories.summary: The first-round rookie might find himself playing another position on Thursday night.
stories.detailText: With only two days to go until their Thursday night game in Chicago, it seems increasingly likely that the New England Patriots will be without both of their starting guards. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, both Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown are “probably” set to miss the game. If that indeed turns out to be the case — and practice participation thus far suggests so — the Patriots have multiple directions they could go in. One of them is inserting their first-round draft pick from earlier this year, Caleb Lomu. “I think that Caleb will have to be ready to go at multiple positions,” Vrabel told reporters on Tuesday. “We were getting ready for him to have to be able to pull the ball in the game, in another different scenario. Where that ends up being on Thursday — he’ll have to be ready for a couple of spots.” Lomu joined the Patriots as the 28th overall selection in this year’s draft after almost exclusively lining up at offensive tackle during his college career at Utah. As executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf said during a press conference shortly after the pick was made, however, the team did see some versatility in him — versatility it continued to explore in the following months. Besides playing both left and right tackle in practice, the 6-foot-6, 308-pounder also saw some reps inside during training camp. The Patriots have not yet had to use him in that capacity during a game, but the injuries suffered on Sunday against the New York Jets might prompt them to reconsider. With Vera-Tucker and Brown unlikely to play due to their respective hamstring and knee injuries, Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor project as the next men up. The two were already inserted into the lineup down the stretch versus the Jets. If there should there be any hiccups against the Bears, however, the Patriots might just end up turning to Lomu. “Everyone’s got to prepare like a starter for those types of things that happen,” the 21-year-old said after the win over the Jets. “It’s terrible to see. It does happen, though, unfortunately, in this league.”

stories.title: 2026 NFL Week 7 Power Rankings: Cowboys continue to plummet
stories.summary: The Cowboys continue to fall in power rankings
stories.detailText: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys refuse to rise to the occasion. Last week it was taking care of business at home against a team they were huge favorites against. While it was more to expect them to travel and emerge victorious as underdogs, the expectation was to at the very least compete. They did not. A month and change ago the national narrative around this team was that they had a very quiet offseason and had built a team that could legitimately challenge to finally end The Drought™. They are fortunate to play in an NFC East this season where they still might win it despite their 2-4 record, but right now they don’t look like they can put an end to anything let alone the shadow that has lived over the franchise for a generation. It will come as no surprise to see that the Cowboys have really fallen in our power rankings and in those from across the internet. On with the show. 1 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 1) It must be nice to be home favorites against a bad team and show up in a way where you dominate them. 2 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 2) If you are a Bills fan you have to be slightly worried that they are peaking too soon, right? Or do only we have those insecurities? 3 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 3) They are back and better than ever. Not really, but Kenneth Walker is such a cheat code for them. 4 – New England Patriots (LW: 6) Reports of their demise were seemingly incorrect! 5 – Detroit Lions (LW: 8) Back from the bye. 6 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 5) It was certainly not idea to lose to the Texans and give them life. They will be alright, though. Travis Hunter is really finding his NFL form. 7 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 4) They need Lamar Jackson back in the worst way. 8 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 16) Deep sigh. Th edeepest of sighs. 9 – Chicago Bears (LW: 11) They almost blew it against Atlanta, but a win is a win and this one came with Caleb Williams so things likely feel more normal than they have in some time. 10 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 15) It feels like we are still sleeping on this team. They are so much fun and have serious offensive firepower. I know that Philly was down, but the Panthers are legit. 11 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 7) They have a quarterback issue, but when you win a Super Bowl (not that we would know what that’s like lately) you are likely less upset when things aren’t going perfectly immediately after. 12 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 9) Also back from some rest. 13 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 10) Them, too! 14 – Houston Texans (LW: 22) It is amazing how good 2-4 must feel to them compared to how it feels to us. 15 – Denver Broncos (LW: 12) Obviously they won, but wow they have serious quarterback problems. It is hard to trust them long-term. 16 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 24) Who would have thought? What a weird surprise! 17 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 17) Mike McCarthy is finding a way. Good for him. 18 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 13) They are very, very far from being the super power they were hyped up to be. 19 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 21) This team is a ton of fun. Maybe they can sneak in as the third Wild Card when it is all said and done. Whatever the case, Klint Kubiak was very clearly the right hire. 20 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 14) Can you believe that they are legitimately getting production out of Kyle Pitts? Finally! 21 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 29) They are definitely going to blow out the Cowboys in a couple of weeks. Right? 22 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 26) Kellen Moore stopped the skid! 23 – New York Giants (LW: 18) The NFC East is terrible, but they might be the least terrible. 24 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 19) They definitely are not. 25 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 20) All the best to Jalen Hurts. 26 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 23) Chris Ballard is finally gone. A selling of assets feels imminent, and likely a head coach change. 27 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 25) So Jalon Daniels isn’t the greatest quarterback of all time? 28 – New York Jets (LW: 27) It was a tough scene that Aaron Glenn did not know that the Jets did not get the ball to start the second half. 29 – Washington Commanders (LW: 28) It was also tough that Dan Quinn did not know when it was a fourth down. 30 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 32) They won a game! 31 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 30) They still have not. 32 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 31) Yikes. ESPN : 20 (LW: 15) Here we go. Biggest issue on offense: Lack of consistency in the running game The Cowboys’ running game is off to its worst start — 456 yards in six games — since 1989, the year before Emmitt Smith showed up. Six different running backs have more total rushing yards than the Cowboys. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but the inconsistency and lack of attempts are killing the offense. Coordinator Klayton Adams said last week the Cowboys are being forced to play with one arm tied behind their back because they can’t run it well enough. That has impacted the passing game, too. Quarterback Dak Prescott was under duress on 21 of his 41 second-half pass attempts against Green Bay, averaging only 4.8 yards per attempt. — Todd Archer NFL.com : 26 (LW: 18) The first line is fair. I’ve lost all faith in the Cowboys. The offense was their lone strength, but it has devolved into a mess of an operation. Their quarterback isn’t adjusting to a consistently messy post-snap picture, and Dallas’ chances of victory have evaporated. We already knew this defense was a problem, but the offense’s regression has escalated this situation from general concern to something bordering on catastrophe. It’s a shame, too, because the NFC East has never been more winnable. As of now, I don’t think it’ll be the Cowboys finishing on top. USA Today : 26 (LW: 24) Another drop. “GOTI,” aka, Greatest Offense There Is? It’s nice to have goals. Not always wise to publicly reveal them. Yahoo : 21 (LW: 20) Only a slight dip here. Nobody questioned the Cowboys’ offense. Through four games Dallas averaged 30.5 points per game and was third in the NFL in EPA per play, trailing only San Francisco and Buffalo. Then, over the last two games, its offense has disappeared against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, neither of which has a great defense. The Cowboys are averaging 14.5 points over their last two games and slipped to 19th in EPA per play. Their defense isn’t good enough to overcome that. “Because of the lack of a running game, we’re a little bit one-sided and the best way to be on offense as a unit is to have balance,” Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said, according to ESPN. The running game is a problem. Dallas has just 98 rushing yards total over the last two games, it has reached 100 yards in a game just once and rank 31st in rushing yards per game. It’s also accurate that the Cowboys looked completely unprepared for a blitz-heavy approach from the Packers, and that could be a coaching issue. Perhaps getting the run game going will dissuade future opponents from blitzing on most downs. CBS Sports : 19 (LW: 17) Still inside the top 20. The offense is suddenly having some issues, which I didn’t see coming. But in their bad division, there is still time to turn it around, starting this week at Philadelphia. The Athletic : 22 (LW: 20) Right behind the Eagles and Giants. The only people associated with the Cowboys who are happy at the moment are Lamb’s fantasy managers. He’s ninth in scoring (21.9 ppg) and third in the league in receiving yards (577). He was targeted 18 times Sunday night and finished with nine catches for 70 yards. ProFootballTalk : 23 (LW: 20) And there it is. Cheap does as cheap is. Week To Week Movement Full Power Rankings

stories.title: Packers Film Room: Matthew Golden rights a past wrong
stories.summary: Breaking down an explosive pass against the Cowboys and looking at how important the small details are.
stories.detailText: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden (0) is tackled by Dallas Cowboys' Shavon Revel Jr. (28) on a 37-yard reception during the first quarter of their game Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There’s not much that makes me sadder than a cool concept that doesn’t pay off, and Green Bay Packers fans saw this in Week 3. Early in the game, the Packers broke out a slick variant of Hank. Hank is a quick game concept, with the outside man running a Hitch route and the inside man running a Flat route. It’s not generally an explosive concept, but it’s been a solid, chain-moving concept for the Packers. On the season, Hank has gained an average of 5.8 YPA and has a success rate of 50%. On this particular version, the receiver who runs the Hitch route is supposed to give a quick cut on the Hitch, then turn upfield on a vertical. It’s a Hitch-and-Go. And, since a Slant-and-Go is called a Sluggo, I’ve been calling this a Huggo. Against the Falcons, Golden is on the Huggo. The play ends with an incomplete pass, with what appears to be a Jordan Love overthrow. It’s a good concept that doesn’t hit. There were a lot of things about that Week 3 game that made me sad, but this was certainly high on the list. Fast forward to this past week: a win against the Cowboys. Midway through the 1st quarter, the Packers tried it again. Once again, Golden is running the Huggo from the outside. There’s some contact as he releases off the line, but he is able to spin cleanly to the outside, away from coverage. This time, it’s a beautiful throw from Jordan Love. He just lays this ball right over Golden’s shoulder, landing as light as a feather. This ended up going for 37 yards. A few plays later, the Packers scored a TD to take a 7-0 lead. We’re not really breaking that down here, but I did want to include it. Golden is on a post and Love is able to hold the safety in place. His feet and shoulders are pointed to the outside, but he opens up on the throw and releases to the middle. The safety is looking for something to his outside shoulder, so the middle is open for Golden. Back to Huggo. Why did it work this week? Was it as simple as the throw being better? We’ve seen this concept a couple times over the years, and the Huggo route was always a pretty quick sell. Quick break on the Hitch then an almost immediate spin in the other direction and a vertical release. Against the Falcons, Golden had a definite stop, sit then spin outside. That’s different than how we had seen it run it in the past. The timing was different. That stop on the Hitch before releasing meant it was longer before Golden was downfield. When I looked at this play in Week 3 , I wondered whether that stop from Golden was a change in the way this was coached, or whether Golden was just taking an extra beat on the route. With what we saw this week, I think we have our answer. Golden cuts on the Hitch then spins and releases quickly. If you look at the videos at the same time, you’ll see that Golden is 4-5 yards downfield against the Cowboys by the time he starts his spin against the Falcons. (Falcons game is on the top, Cowboys on the bottom.) It’s small, but the details matter. They got it nailed down against the Cowboys and it led to a big play. stories.detailText: New York Giants linebacker Trace Ford makes a tackle against the Washington Commanders. | Getty Images The NY Giants are signing edge defender Trace Ford to their 53-man linebacker, per a report from Dan Duggan . Ford, 25, was originally signed by the Giants as an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma after the 2025 NFL Draft. He spent that year on the Giants practice squad and was signed to a reserve/futures contract for the 2026 season. Ford was elevated to the active roster in each of the last three games and was a part of an active rotation. Ford has been impressive in the preseason and has earned the trust of the Giants coaches. He was the first man off the bench to spell both Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux against both the Arizona Cardinals and New Orleans Saints. Ford might not have the rare size-athleticism combination boasted by the Giants starting linebackers, but he’s solid in both categories and plays with a wide-open motor. Ford takes the place of veteran Jihad Ward, who was released by the Giants earlier on Tuesday.

stories.detailText: (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs brought in rookie linebacker Aiden Fisher, a teammate of left tackle Kahlil Benson at Indiana last season, for a workout. Jason Anderson of 810 Sports was the first to report that he was expected to sign with the Chiefs’ practice squad , and NFL Insider Jordan Schultz backed that up by reporting that he will be signing with Kansas City . Listed at 6 feet 1 inch and 231 pounds, Fisher was the 13th-ranked linebacker in the 2026 NFL Draft, according to draft expert Dane Brugler of The Athletic . During his time with the Hoosiers, Fisher totaled 215 tackles, 16 tackles for loss, six sacks, two interceptions, one forced fumble and five passes defended. The comparison to Tranquill speaks to Fisher’s potential as an all-around linebacker who can make plays against the pass and run. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Packers fans and fans across the country. The Green Bay Packers have the most prolific receiving duo in the NFL this season. No pair of teammates has combined for more receiving yards than Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to this point in the season, as each of the two star receivers have eclipsed 500 yards in just six games so far. Of course, he could have had a few more big plays if not for some uncharacteristic drops on Sunday, as the yardage he left on the field should have pushed him up into the team lead. The back-and-forth between these two players has us wondering which player Packers fans think will win this friendly battle at the end of the season. stories.title: 10 Thoughts on the NFL: Eagles failed Jalen Hurts, Travis Hunter Emerges, Bad QBs, and more
stories.summary: A lot went down in Week 6 in the NFL, and @kdthompson5 has some thoughts on it. Ten, to be exact.
stories.detailText: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Jalen Hurts of Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images 1. Even if this story wasn’t personal for you—and it unfortunately is for me—you should be infuriated with the Philadelphia Eagles for allowing Jalen Hurts to risk his life for a football game in London two weekends ago. They reportedly flew him to London with a superficial clot in his left calf, then kept him awake for 36 hours for fear of the clot traveling to his lungs and potentially killing him, then allowed him to play a football game in which hard contact to his leg could’ve dislodged that clot and killed him anyway. Whether a doctor works for a football team or not shouldn’t matter. The oath says, “Do no harm.” That sometimes means making those hyper-competitive humans take a seat for their own well-being. They’re lucky their decision to green-light him to play only cost Hurts’ season, maybe his career, rather than his life. Regardless, someone needs to be held accountable for this. 2. Passing charts have turned into the new box-score watching for quarterback evaluation, and Caleb Williams’ game on Sunday is just the latest example. Except that, even if you didn’t watch the game, you should be able to see the difference between Williams going 30-for-26 for 305 yards and a touchdown versus Bo Nix barely topping 107 yards on 27 throws, right? There are multiple ways to have a really good game as an NFL quarterback. Taking risks and throwing the ball into tight windows down the field—something Williams has proven time and again he can do—is one way. Taking what the opposing defense gives you when they’re clearly trying to take away the deep part of the field, which is what Williams did yesterday, is another. The bottom line: if you don’t like a guy and want to see him fail, just say so. Don’t pretend to be objective. In the end, you’re mad that Williams now leads the league in completion percentage, which means you can’t use that argument against him to defend your fav. Cry more. 3. Personally, I have no problem with what Ryan Fitzpatrick said about Nix after the Broncos quarterback’s Thursday night performance in an overtime win against Seattle. And sure, maybe it is a little biased because I never thought highly of Nix coming into the league, plus he might still be rounding into form after the injury he suffered last year. But pretending he’s doing anything else but playing objectively terrible football is just wrong right now. If this were any other third-year quarterback averaging 174 passing yards a game, we would say that guy isn’t an NFL starter, record be damned. Why should Nix get a pass? 4. Y’all might find this mean, but I don’t care: L.J. Collier celebrating after recovering a fumble and getting tackled on that Rams two-point conversion attempt makes me mad. You cost your team two points because you wouldn’t give the ball up to a faster player who would’ve scored, and you’re happy about it? Someone lower his Madden Awareness rating to -2. That man’s lucky those two points didn’t come back to bite his team. 5. Remember back when Chris Ballard and Ryan Pace were both up for the Chicago Bears general manager job all those years ago? Wild to see Ballard finally out in Indianapolis after all that time, with the Colts just relieving him of his duties after their latest loss. This isn’t to disparage either of those two or Pace’s successor, Ryan Poles, but to point out the truth in something Ballard pointed out after Andrew Luck’s retirement: hitting on the quarterback is everything. Pace failed at it with both Mitchell Trubisky and Justin Fields. Ballard struggled to replace Luck but ultimately squeezed enough out of veterans to keep him employed until this year. And Poles arguably would’ve been fired already if not for landing Caleb Williams, which has helped people forget his misses at other positions. Remember that. 6. Thanks to the aforementioned Colts, there will be no 0-17 season this year. And I really do mean “Thanks to the Colts,” because the Tennessee Titans’ offense putting up 26 points on 186 yards of total offense is just offensive. Cam Ward’s 102 passing yards marked the fewest this season for a winning starting quarterback who played the entire game. There’s so much wrong with that team that it’s hard sometimes to parse between Ward being bad and everything else around him being awful. At least they know they’re not about to make the wrong kind of history. 7. In other news: maybe Ben Johnson and the Bears offense really are that good (when healthy). Remember that 59-point outing they put on the Carolina Panthers in Week 1 that had us all questioning what planet we were living on? Turns out Carolina has literally been one of the best units in the league since that point, holding opponents to just 16 points per game following that season opener. The NFL can change so dramatically from week to week that any one game can’t be taken as a complete picture of what a team is. For example, that next week against the Vikings on a rainy day, the Bears looked disgustingly bad. But who doesn’t want to believe the Bears could just randomly drop 60 on any defense they choose? 9. Count me among the people who questioned whether Travis Hunter could legitimately be a factor as a cornerback and wide receiver after starring in both roles at the University of Colorado a few years ago. As it turns out…he can. And is. According to NFL Communications, Hunter is the third player since 1970 with a touchdown reception and interception in the same game, joining Pro Football Hall of Famer Brian Dawkins (Sept. 29, 2002 with Philadelphia) and Roy Green (Sept. 20, 1981 with the St. Louis Cardinals). Shoutout to Liam Coen for having the gumption to actually use him in both roles and being creative enough to pull it off. What a player. 10. Question for the group: when’s the last time you saw a player fall off harder than Justin Herbert? And no, you don’t get to say “he was always bad,” because he wasn’t. Nothing approaching this, certainly. I’m having a hard time thinking of anyone. But we don’t have to ask that question about coaching falloffs, because Jim Harbaugh does it every four years. His flamout just arrived a year early this time.

stories.title: The Chiefs’ schedule gets a lot tougher starting in Week 7
stories.summary: Kansas City has taken advantage of a soft schedule so far. Can they keep the winning going?
stories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard to deny that the (5-0) Kansas City Chiefs had a favorable schedule to begin the 2026 regular season. The best opponent so far has been the (4-2) Denver Broncos , who were clearly caught off guard by the Chiefs’ shift in offensive identity in the season-opening beatdown on “Monday Night Football.” It’s reasonable to believe Denver would have put together a more competitive game with even just one game of this year’s film to study. The team’s other four opponents have a combined 5-18 record going into Week 7. The Chiefs have taken care of business on a light schedule, as shown by the second-best point differential in the NFL (+57). Only the (6-0) San Francisco 49ers (+67) are better at this point. That’s what elite teams do, but the schedule will get a lot harder from here. The road trips So far, the team has hit the road to play the winless Miami Dolphins and to play the Las Vegas Raiders at “Arrowhead West,” where Chiefs head coach Andy Reid is the venue’s winningest coach. Starting in Week 7, the road trips get longer and more difficult. The “Sunday Night Football” road game against the (3-3) Seattle Seahawks will feature a defending Super Bowl champion and its roaring crowd, who could feel like they’re backed into a corner with a .500 record after six weeks. The Chiefs can expect an A-game from Seattle in every phase, including the drive to shut down the NFL’s leading rusher, Kenneth Walker. He was the Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks less than a year ago, and has been the driving force for Kansas City’s success on offense this year. After the primetime game on the West Coast, the Broncos will welcome the Chiefs to Mile High for a pivotal matchup. Let’s say Kansas City drops its first game of the season in Seattle while Denver takes care of the (2-4) Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Suddenly, Week 8 could put the AFC West teams at the same level in the standings. If the Chiefs emerge from the next two road games still unbeaten, they will have built up a lot of margin for error for the next significant stretch of away games: starting on Thanksgiving night in Week 12, Kansas City will play the (5-1) Buffalo Bills , (2-4) Los Angeles Rams — on “Thursday Night Football” — and (3-2) Cincinnati Bengals before finally returning to Arrowhead four days before Christmas. Six of the team’s next eight games are on the road. The strength of opponents Going into the season, we knew the Chiefs’ schedule got a lot tougher starting in Week 7. From this point on, the team will face seven teams that made the postseason last year. Between now and the Week 17 rematch with the Chargers, only four teams currently have losing records — and one of them is a sleeping giant in the Rams. Kansas City still has to play the undefeated 49ers, the one-loss Bills and three other teams with only two losses in the AFC playoff race: the Broncos, Bengals and the New England Patriots . This all happens before the final two-game stretch against the Chargers and Raiders. The bottom line The Chiefs are clearly one of the best teams in the NFL this season, ranking top-10 in points and yards on both sides of the ball. However, they’ve faced a much lighter schedule than Kansas City will face for the rest of the season, with no bye week to rest in the middle of a postseason run. The team has built up some margin for error with an undefeated start, but it will need to keep winning to earn the sole bye week in the AFC playoff bracket.

stories.title: Detroit Lions kick off Packers week with full attendance at practice
stories.summary: The Detroit Lions are entering Packers week with full participation in practice.
stories.detailText: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16), offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (70), left, and center Seth McLaughlin (65), quarterback Luke Altmyer (2) practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday August 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions will have their first division game of the season this Sunday, hosting the 4-2 Green Bay Packers at Ford Field for a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Detroit got a head start on the week, moving their first practice from Wednesday to Tuesday, a common practice from this regime out of a bye week. According to coach Dan Campbell, it also served the purpose of giving returning players Brian Branch and Cade Mays a big load of work, then giving them—and the rest of the team—Wednesday off to let their bodies recover. “That’s one of the reasons why we’re practicing tomorrow and not Wednesday,” Campbell said Monday. “So, we can push some of these guys a little bit knowing they’re going into a day off. I think that’ll help a little bit.” And if Tuesday’s practice is any indication, the Lions will be entering this pivotal Week 7 matchup with a good bill of health. Not only will Branch and Mays make their 2026 debuts for the team, but Detroit’s Tuesday practice had every single player on the active roster practicing. That includes the return of reserve cornerback Rock Ya-Sin, who had missed last game with a hamstring injury. Now, it wouldn’t be completely accurate to call the Lions “fully healthy” at this point in the season. Just last week, the Lions placed three players—WR Tom Kennedy, G Ben Bartch, and LB Devin White—on injured reserve , with Kennedy out for the season and White out for at least a couple of months with a broken forearm. Beyond that, the Lions still have Isiah Pacheco, Kendrick Law, Avonte Maddox, and Thomas Harper on injured reserve as well. Still, thus far, the Lions’ injury luck has certainly been better than in previous years, and they’ll need all hands on deck for a surging Packers team this week and an undefeated Vikings squad waiting in Week 8. We’ll have a more thorough injury report on Wednesday, when the Lions are expected to drop their first official practice designations of the week.

stories.title: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin has torn patellar tendon, ending his season
stories.summary: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon, an injury that will end his season, coach Dan Quinn announced Tuesday.
stories.detailText: Washington Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin tore the patellar tendon in his left knee and will miss the remainder of the season, coach Dan Quinn said. McLaurin suffered the injury late in the first quarter of Monday's 23-17 loss at San Francisco. The injury also calls into question his future with the Commanders. "Man, he brings a lot on and off the field," Quinn said. "It's a big hit, and we'll lean on a number of guys." McLaurin, 31, leads Washington with 230 yards receiving on 15 receptions. He finished with one catch for 27 yards Monday. But with two minutes, 16 seconds left in the opening quarter, McLaurin was injured while cutting on a route; the play ended with a sack of quarterback Jayden Daniels . McLaurin also missed a Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts after injuring his hamstring two days before the game, but he returned a week later. He sat out seven games in 2025, ending a streak of 72 consecutive games played. Before last season, he had been a consistent producer, with five consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, from 2020 to 2024. He has been the emotional engine of Washington's offense since joining the team as a third-round pick in 2019. He also was named a captain for this season. McLaurin became a fan favorite and a face for the franchise during a turbulent period that featured five losing seasons in his first seven years; multiple investigations into the franchise and former team owner Dan Snyder and a sale of the team. McLaurin also played with 13 different starting quarterbacks until Daniels arrived in 2024. It was the first time he played with the same opening day starter in consecutive seasons. But now McLaurin's future with Washington could be in jeopardy. He signed a three-year extension in 2025 after missing all of training camp during negotiations. The deal allowed Washington to either release him after the season or to restructure. Otherwise, he would count $34 million against the salary cap and $39.5 million in 2028. If he is released, Washington would save approximately $8.5 million on the cap next year. The Commanders can use several receivers to compensate for McLauren's absence, including Treylon Burks , Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams . Stefon Diggs has started opposite McLaurin.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are in the midst of a three-game losing streak after falling to the Buffalo Bills 33-30 on Sunday. However, that didn’t impact the Raiders’ standing in the Week 7 NFL Power Rankings roundup, as many in the media are giving quarterback Kirk Cousins his flowers. Bleacher Report 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 18 Here’s how most people expected this season to go for the Raiders: Kirk Cousins would open the season as the starter under center, but as the losses mounted, the reins in the offense would be handed to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. The Raiders have dropped three straight, but don’t hold your breath waiting for Mendoza to take over. For the second time in three weeks, the Raiders gave an AFC heavyweight all they could handle in Week 6. Cousins was a big reason why, lighting up the Bills for 313 passing yards. It’s going to come down to the Raiders’ priorities. Once the team’s unlikely postseason hopes have been dashed, then odds are we’ll see Mendoza take over. But given how feisty these Raiders have been to date, those playoff aspirations may be around a while longer than we thought. — Gary Davenport Davenport is correct in that the 3-0 start has altered the timeline (or at least expectation) of when the rookie will take over behind center in Las Vegas. But it does feel like this weekend could be a swing game, even though the team would only be one game below .500 and still in playoff contention if it doesn’t leave Los Angeles with a win. A loss to a struggling and hobbled Los Angeles Rams would make it four in a row for the Raiders, meaning they aren’t able to beat the best teams they’ve played even when Cousins is playing well. At that point, the postseason odds become very bleak, and it might be time to start focusing on 2027 and beyond for the rest of 2026. The Athletic 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 17 Fantasy focus: Kirk Cousins The 38-year-old quarterback just keeps hanging on, but the calls for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will get louder after the Raiders dropped their third straight game Sunday. That’s not necessarily Cousins’ fault, though. He is 29th in fantasy scoring (18.5 ppg) after being drafted No. 264 overall. Tight end Brock Bowers is once again pacing the Raiders offense. He’s 13th in scoring (20.6 ppg). — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff This basically reiterates the point above. Cousins is playing well, but at some point, the organization’s and coaching staff’s focus needs to shift to the future. Getting over the hump and taking down the Rams this Sunday will buy the veteran quarterback and the Raiders’ playoff hopes some time, but the club has used up all of its moral victories when it comes to the current starting lineup and the outlook for the 2026 season. Sports Illustrated 19. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 16 Piggybacking on [the Browns potentially trading for a quarterback], an interesting thought experiment: What if the Raiders decided that Fernando Mendoza was ready? Would the Browns be at all interested in having Cousins back up/challenge Deshaun Watson for snaps down the stretch, especially if Cleveland keeps gutting out victories? — Conor Orr In my opinion, this feels more like a fantasy idea than a trade that can actually happen. I have a hard time seeing Kubiak sending away Mendoza’s mentor right after making the rookie the starter. Part of the reason Cousins was brought in was to add a veteran voice to the quarterback room, giving Mendoza another person to turn to for advice. In other words, Cousins would still provide value to the team even if he isn’t on the field. Also, while Watson isn’t exactly lighting it up in Cleveland, I have a hard time seeing the Browns trade for a quarterback and have that quarterback pick up Todd Monken’s offense quickly enough to make a change, especially since the team is winning. NFL.com 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 19 Another tough loss marked the Raiders’ third straight defeat, dropping them from a 3-0 start to 3-3 after six weeks. For some teams, this might be a sign of crisis. These Raiders, however, have proven competitive in two of those three losses, going blow for blow with two AFC titans in the Chiefs and Bills. This is part of the process of evolving from cellar-dweller to aspiring contender, in which the upstart learns how to win the close battles against proven teams. Las Vegas has received a couple of good lessons in this department recently, while Kirk Cousins continues to thrive. There are no moral victories, but there are degrees of losses, and this one appears more favorable than others. — Nick Shook I like this assessment of where the franchise is heading. Would it have been better to pull off upsets instead of losing by three points to the Chiefs and Bills? Absolutely, no one is arguing that. But the Silver and Black are at least making strides and are clearly a better team than they were last year. Rome wasn’t built in a day, and remember, Kansas City took pity on Vegas in the first meeting last season. The Chiefs didn’t even throw the ball in the fourth quarter and took a knee before the two-minute warning, and that was a bad Chiefs team for their standards. ESPN 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 17 Biggest issue on offense: Run blocking Las Vegas signed center Tyler Linderbaum with the expectation that he would fix the team’s run-blocking issues from last season. Instead, those have continued, especially Sunday, when the Raiders totaled just 65 rushing yards. The unit struggled containing the Bills’ offensive line; Linderbaum had a hard time blocking defensive tackle Deone Walker. Caleb Rogers, who started at right guard over Jackson Powers-Johnson, also whiffed on a block that led to Ashton Jeanty being stopped for a 3-yard loss at the goal line in the fourth quarter. — Ryan McFadden Fair or not, Linderbaum was supposed to be the catalyst to solve this problem, hence the record-setting contract. Instead, the results are about the same, and the center has been average to slightly above average. But don’t take my word for it; take his. Linderbaum was very candid about his performance against the Bills and said he “has to play better for the team.”

teamStories.detailText: Kyle Terada-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Raiders are considered one of the “nomads of the NFL” for good reason. The franchise has moved four times and called three different cities home (Oakland, Los Angeles, Oakland again, and now Las Vegas). The Las Vegas Raiders have spent seven seasons in their new location, which happens to be one of the biggest tourist destinations in the country. Whether it’s Raiders fans from Oakland, Los Angeles, another part of the world, or opposing fans looking to attend an away game, that leads to many circling a date to visit Las Vegas in the fall. But where should you stay, what is there to do, where should you eat, and how do you get to the game in the “Entertainment Capital of the World”? Places to stay in Las Vegas The Strip is the most convenient choice. Allegiant Stadium technically isn’t on The Strip, but it’s right off of it. If you’re the fancy type, Mandalay Bay is a good choice since it’s close to the stadium, while the Luxor and Excalibur are in the same vicinity but are more budget-friendly options. However, just about any hotel on The Strip is going to get pricey during a game weekend. So, you might want to look into places like the Holiday Inn Express or Staybridge Suites, which are off The Strip to help save some money but still within walking distance to Allegiant. If you want to escape the hustle and bustle of Las Vegas, the M Resort in Henderson is actually the official team headquarters hotel for the Raiders. It’s a lot quieter and near the team’s practice facility, though you will need a car to get to the game. The M also has a Raiders-themed restaurant in it. Another thing to consider: The Strip is considered a “tourist trap”. Most locals stay away from it because everything is marked up, including the table minimums at the casino. There’s a lot more going on there, but you’re going to pay a premium for it. Things to do in Las Vegas Well, it’s Vegas, baby! Of course, there are casinos everywhere you look. Even if you aren’t a gambler typically, there is a “when in Rome” type of vibe to Las Vegas where people put at least a few bucks on the table or in a slot machine with the hopes of paying for their trip and/or bringing home some extra cash. Just remember, those palaces weren’t built on winners! Also, there are plenty of shows to catch if you’re looking for something on the entertainment side. You can find pretty much any sort of live entertainment that you can think of, ranging from the acrobatics of Cirque du Soleil to comedy and magic. Additionally, the Sphere is a newer venue that typically has some type of concert, live event or movie going on . It just depends on what they have scheduled during your visit. So, there’s a chance what’s going on at the Sphere during the time of your visit isn’t something you’re interested in. But the venue and experience itself is worth checking out, and it’s more family-friendly than the casino or most shows. On that note, the Mandalay Bay hotel has an aquarium , and Circus Circus has a theme park in it if you’re traveling with and looking for something to do with your kids. Additionally, there are several different options to tour the Grand Canyon , which is about a two- to two-and-a-half hour drive from Vegas, or the Hoover Dam , a 45-minute to an hour drive. To be honest, you’d have to try pretty hard to be bored in Las Vegas… Best places to eat in Las Vegas If you’re on the Strip, you can find just about any type of restaurant you’re looking for. Not only does it cover every cuisine (sushi, BBQ, Italian, etc.), but it also ranges from recognizable fast food options to local steakhouses. Granted, it might be some of the most expensive fast food you’ll ever pay for, but that’s just the Strip. If it’s your first time out west, it’s a requirement to stop at In-N-Out for a burger. There’s a location on the Strip, as well as a handful in the surrounding areas. My go-to order is a three-by-three (three patties and three slices of cheese) with grilled onions and extra spread (their 1000 Island-like sauce), fries and a chocolate-strawberry milkshake. I will say In-N-Out’s fries are underwhelming, but the burgers and shakes are top-notch. Sometimes, I’ll skip the fries and just do two burgers. Also, make sure to check out the “ not so secret menu ” and ask for well-done fries if you like them crispy. Additionally, there are plenty of buffets. The go-to, in my opinion, is the one at the Bellagio . However, it’s only open from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. during the week and dinner is only available on the weekend — Saturday Seafood dinner ($69.99) and Sunday ($59.99). A weekday brunch will run you about $45 a person, and it’s about $50 on the weekend. Children under five get in free, and six to 11 are half off. That’s expensive for a buffet, but it isn’t your typical buffet food, and it has cuisine options from all over the world. In the mood for something fancier? Gallagher’s Steakhouse in the New York New York hotel is my top choice. I’ve also heard good things about TENDER Steakhouse in the Luxor (which is a more affordable option for a steakhouse), and SW Steakhouse in the Wynn (one of the pricier options). If you want to get away from the Strip (and save some money), Eater has 18 places to eat that are away from the touristy part of town. Two of the more popular options are Esther’s Kitchen and Herbs & Rye . Allegiant Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options It depends on where you’re staying, even if you’re on the Strip, since it’s over four miles long. Allegiant Stadium is on the very South end of the Strip. So, if you’re at Mandalay Bay, Luxor, Excalibur, MGM Grand or Aria, it’s an easy walk. Also, there are several pedestrian bridges to make the trek safer and avoid traffic. You can’t miss them either, as the bridges are right in your face. If you’re staying in the middle or the north end of the Strip, the Las Vegas Monorail is a great option to get to the game. Its final station on the south side is at MGM, where you just have to make that short walk, and there are seven stations where you can catch it along the Strip. Children under five years old can ride for free, and single rides for everyone else start at $5. You can also just buy a full-day pass if you want to use the monorail to explore the city, too. If you’re not on the Strip at all, check the RTC website for a few options to take a bus to the game. They have pickup and return options throughout the surrounding areas, including at the M Resort mentioned above, North Las Vegas and near Summerlin. It’s only $4 for a round trip and drops you off right at the stadium. Otherwise, there are always plenty of Ubers, Lyfts or taxis available to get you there. Just be aware of surge pricing. Tailgating at Allegiant Stadium To be honest, the Raiders sacrificed a good tailgate scene when the franchise moved from Oakland to Las Vegas. The B Lot barbeques are a thing of the past, and there simply isn’t enough real estate where Allegiant Stadium is located to have an old-school tailgate. The Raiders do have a ‘ Modelo Tailgate Zone ’ that’s free to enter and has different activities going on, a variety of food and beer/cocktail options, and NFL RedZone playing if you want to hang out in the stadium parking lot before the game. But it’s not nearly the party Oakland tailgates were back in the day. To put it in perspective, the Oakland Coliseum has about 10,000 parking spaces while Allegiant has just 2,700. Essentially, the move to Vegas swapped out a traditional tailgate experience for a unique one with the casinos on the Strip. The Allegiant Stadium Experience If you’re looking to enhance your experience at the game, Allegiant Stadium has several premium clubs and lounges available . They vary from field-level experiences to 200-level options with table seating. You just have to be willing to open up your wallet pretty wide to have those experiences. When you get hungry and/or thirsty, Winna.com recently ranked the Raiders and Allegiant as the fourth-best food and beverage option in the NFL. There’s a wide variety of choices too, ranging from typical stadium food like hot dogs or burgers to gourmet and specialty items like chicken and waffles or focaccia and lox sandwiches. Also, it’s the only NFL stadium that has its own Taco Bell Cantina!

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 6 had the Las Vegas Raiders dropping their third straight game , falling to the Buffalo Bills 33-30 . But let’s see how the weekend fared for a few old friends: Foster Moreau, Davante Adams and Tre’von Moehrig. Foster Moreau Score: 34-31 Texans win Stats: 2 catches, 7 yards, 2 TDs This was a crazy game across the pond to get Sunday started, with the Houston Texans getting a huge divisional win to keep their hopes of an AFC South title alive. Moreau was a big part of that, hauling in a pair of scores as a red zone threat. Granted, those were his only targets in the game, as the 2019 fourth-round pick continues to be a blocking tight end in Houston. Including Sunday, Moreau has 11 catches for 72 yards and three touchdowns this season. Maybe I only find this interesting but the Jags call timeout just before the snap and CJ Stroud still throws it to Foster Moreau and he casually catches the ball with one hand. And then they run the real play after the timeout… pic.twitter.com/eDaDKDmM3Z — Goodberry (@JoeGoodberry) October 18, 2026 Davante Adams Score: 18-16 Rams lose Stats: 3 catches, 39 yards It’s been a while since we’ve checked in on Adams, and now feels like a good time to see how the campaign is going for the wideout. Short answer: not well. The Los Angeles Rams are easily the NFL’s biggest disappointment at 2-4, and dropping a game to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday feels like the icing on that cake. Meanwhile, Adams had a productive two-game stretch in Weeks 2 and 3, with 23 catches for 332 yards and two touchdowns in those contests. However, he’s been held below 55 yards in every other game. On top of that, Adams ruptured a hamstring and will be out for the next six to 10 weeks, according to The Athletic’s Nate Atkins , meaning the former Raider will miss next week’s revenge game. Tre’von Moehrig Score: 25-14 Panthers win Stats: 4 tackles, 0.5 sack, 1 TFL, 2 QB hits This was a big win for the Carolina Panthers, taking down the Philadelphia Eagles to move to 3-2 and sit atop the NFC South standings. Meanwhile, Moehrig managed to make an impact in a few areas of the defense. He’s been having a solid year, collecting 17 tackles in five games and two run stuffs. The 2021 second-round pick has yet to record a PBU or interception in 2026, though.

Trade talks involving Knecht fell through, so the Lakers made a clean break. Knecht was the 17th pick in 2024 and averaged 4.2 points in about 10 minutes a game last season.

headlines.summary: Julian Strawther hurt his left knee in the third quarter of a preseason game against the Clippers on 16 October, when his leg was caught under his body. Denver has diagnosed a left knee sprain, and he will miss the opener against Oklahoma City on 22 October. He will be re-evaluated in about six weeks to see whether he can resume basketball activities. Strawther was the 29th overall pick in 2023, has started 18 games and averaged 7.2 points over 57 appearances last season.

headlines.title: Spurs open with a three-guard lineup

The three guards made their debut together in the 126–97 preseason win over the Kings, where Harper scored 19 points and Fox added 16 points and six rebounds. headlines.summary: Davante Adams ruptured a hamstring and will miss six to 10 weeks, coach Sean McVay said. Poona Ford is out for the season with a ruptured triceps, and Kobie Turner will miss four to six weeks with a groin injury. Kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL on a kickoff and has been placed on injured reserve, a week after the Rams signed him to replace Harrison Mevis. Myles Garrett has played just one game since his offseason trade and is on injured reserve with a knee injury.

headlines.title: Jalen Hurts expected to miss the season with blood clots
headlines.summary: Sources told NFL Network and ESPN that doctors found multiple blood clots in Hurts' lungs. The Eagles and his agent say he has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, and that he is clinically stable with no significant functional limitations. Treatment with blood thinners is expected to keep the three-time Pro Bowler sidelined for at least three months. The Eagles say they expect a full recovery and that he can return to contact football once he is off the medication.

headlines.title: Giants still undecided at QB after McCarthy nearly rallies
headlines.summary: Coach John Harbaugh said Monday he is 'honing in on' a decision between J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston for Sunday's road game against the Texans. McCarthy, who arrived in a trade from Minnesota late last month, came off the bench against the Saints with about 12 minutes left and threw for 243 yards. He led three scoring drives, but the Giants fell 34–27. Winston had 152 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions in the same game.

headlines.title: Patriots lose Romeo Doubs to injured reserve
headlines.summary: Romeo Doubs landed hard on his right shoulder after a diving 42-yard touchdown catch in Sunday's 26–19 win over the Jets, and he has been placed on injured reserve. He will miss at least four games, starting Thursday night at Chicago. This season he has 14 catches for 261 yards and three touchdowns, the most receiving yards on the team. The move came the same week New England activated A.J. Brown from injured reserve.

headlines.title: Bears hold off Falcons with Caleb Williams back
headlines.summary: Caleb Williams returned from injury and completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown in Chicago's 31–23 win over Atlanta. The Bears led 21–7 with 8:48 left in the third quarter, and the Falcons made it competitive late, with Michael Penix Jr. throwing three touchdowns. Kyler Gordon had three sacks and four tackles for Chicago. The game was overshadowed when Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was carted off with a neck injury. The team said he was alert and had movement in all his extremities, and he was taken to hospital for further evaluation.

headlines.title: Maye throws three touchdowns as Patriots hold off Jets
headlines.summary: Drake Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns, his third straight game with at least three TD passes. New England won 26–19 despite losing right tackle Morgan Moses (ankle), left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and right guard Ben Brown (knee) to injuries. Charles Woods picked off Geno Smith in the fourth quarter, Geno Smith's first interception of the season. A.J. Brown returned from injured reserve with three catches for 27 yards and three drops. The Patriots have won three straight and 19 of their last 21 meetings with the Jets.

headlines.title: Travis Hunter's big day in a Jaguars loss
headlines.summary: Travis Hunter had an interception and a touchdown catch in the same game at Wembley, the first player to do that since 2002. It wasn't enough, as Jacksonville lost 34–31 to Houston. Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdowns and one interception, and Jakobi Meyers had 83 receiving yards. Hunter has been used on offence in a specific package this season, and coach Liam Coen has said his usage could change week to week.

headlines.title: Eagles' injuries pile up in loss to Panthers
headlines.summary: Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score, as Carolina beat Philadelphia 25–14. The Eagles were already without Saquon Barkley (right hamstring), and Jordan Davis left the game with an injury. Philadelphia has lost four straight and is 2–4.
